m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series (pre-game through close)
m.quote_history.mechanism: The market's own price path aggregates information (injury news, lineup confirmation, sharp flow) and defines the executable price at each decision time.
m.quote_history.rationale: Quote history is the only way to know what price was actually available at the decision timestamp, to measure line moves against injury-report vintages, and to separate stale quotes from real information. Subtle: last-trade prints on thin NBA prop rungs can be hours old, so mid-of-bid-ask with a staleness flag is safer than last price; and any model input must be joined point-in-time to a quote vintage, never to a closing price.
m.quote_history.measurement: Store every candlestick/snapshot with exchange timestamp and retrieval timestamp. Features: mid, spread, time since last trade, move since open, move in the 90 minutes before tip, move conditional on a news event. Join model features as-of (<= quote time).
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine how much size can be filled at the quoted price and how large the round-trip cost is.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: A mispricing smaller than the half-spread plus fee is not tradable. NBA player-prop rungs far from the main line are often wide and thin, so apparent edges there are frequently untradable. Depth also signals market-maker confidence: a quote that collapses in size near tip often precedes lineup news.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Per rung: best bid/ask, size at best, cumulative size within 2c and 5c, spread in cents and as fraction of price; time-weighted averages over the last hour before tip.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Traded volume and open interest proxy for how much information and how many informed participants have priced the market.
m.volume_oi.rationale: Higher-volume main lines (star player points, game spread) tend to be better arbitraged than thin alternate rungs, so the same model edge should be discounted differently by liquidity. Open interest growth through the day also indicates when the market is still absorbing news. Subtle: volume is cumulative and includes both sides, so use deltas around events.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Cumulative and per-hour volume, open interest, number of distinct trade prints; rank of the rung within its event by volume; ratio of volume to open interest.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: A strike ladder is a set of tail probabilities of one underlying count; consistency across rungs exposes mispriced rungs and reveals the market's implied distribution.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Over/under ladders (e.g. points 15+/20+/25+/30+) must be monotone non-increasing, and the implied pmf (differences between rungs) shows where the market puts mass. Rungs are heavily correlated, so a model edge on 25+ is largely the same bet as on 30+; position sizing must treat the ladder as one exposure. Also reveals integer-vs-half-point structure and whether the market's implied variance is wider or narrower than a count model.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Extract all rungs for the same player/stat/game, enforce monotonicity, difference to get implied P(X=k), fit mean and dispersion; flag rungs whose price is off the fitted curve by more than spread+fee; compute rung correlation for exposure netting.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: The realized outcome and settlement timestamp are the ground truth the whole backtest is scored against.
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Needed for calibration and hit-rate work but never a pregame input. Subtle: NBA box scores are occasionally corrected after the game (assist, rebound, steal credit), and Kalshi settles on a defined source/time, so the settled value can differ from a later-corrected box score; labels must come from the contract settlement, not a re-scraped box score.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Pull settled value, result, settlement time per market; reconcile with the box score source named in the rules; flag disagreements and late changes.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)
NBA live box score (cdn.nba.com liveData boxscore, free)

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement, void)
m.rules_text.mechanism: Contract wording determines what event is being predicted: whether overtime counts, how DNP or postponement resolves, push handling, and which stat source governs.
m.rules_text.rationale: The same basketball outcome can map to different payouts depending on wording: overtime-inclusive totals shift the total by roughly the OT probability times about 10 points; player props may void or settle No on DNP; period markets may exclude OT. A model fitted on the wrong settlement definition is systematically biased. Wording can differ between series and change over time, so version it per market.
m.rules_text.measurement: Snapshot rules_primary / rules_secondary text per market with hash; parse flags: ot_included, dnp_rule (void vs No), postponement_rule, tie_rule, source_of_truth, strike inclusivity (> vs >=).
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sportsbook lines are an independent, highly liquid estimate of the same distribution and embed information (injuries, sharp money) that fundamentals miss.
m.external_lines.rationale: For NBA sides and totals the sharp closing line is hard to beat; for player props it is a strong prior on the mean and distribution. The informative quantity is the disagreement between Kalshi and the book after removing vig, and whether the book moved first. Subtle: timestamps must be point-in-time and props are often posted/stale at different times than main lines.
m.external_lines.measurement: De-vig each book line (multiplicative or power), convert to implied mean/probability, track open-to-now movement and cross-book dispersion; compute Kalshi minus consensus per rung with staleness flags.
free_sources: The Odds API (free tier, limited credits; sportsbook lines)
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force
m.fees.mechanism: Fees convert a model probability edge into an expected net return and vary with price.
m.fees.rationale: The fee is a function of price (largest near 50c), so the minimum edge required differs by rung: a 2c edge can be profitable on a 10c longshot and negative at 50c. The schedule can change and differs for maker vs taker orders, so it must be versioned.
m.fees.measurement: Versioned fee formula per series; net edge = model p - price - fee(price) for taker, with maker rebate/fee where applicable; breakeven edge by price bucket.
free_sources: Kalshi fee schedule document (kalshi.com, free) and API fee fields

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: Market open, close, halt and postponement events define when information can still be traded on and when a market is void.
m.lifecycle.rationale: NBA markets may close at tip or stay open into play; a lineup surprise after close cannot be traded, and postponed games void or extend. Determining the true last tradable time per market is required for point-in-time discipline.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Record open_time, close_time, expected_expiration, status transitions with timestamps; compute minutes between last injury-report update and close; flag postponed or rescheduled games.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung per family (from settlements)
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Empirical hit rates by rung reveal systematic miscalibration of the market in that family (favorite-longshot, over bias) independent of any fundamentals model.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: If 30+ point rungs priced at 12c hit 9% over a large sample, that is a calibration finding that stands without a player model. Subtle: rungs on one game are correlated, so effective sample size is the number of games not markets, and hit rates must be conditioned on price bucket and line vintage.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: From settled markets: realized frequency vs mean price by price bucket, by strike distance from the book mean, by family and season; bootstrap by game for intervals.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time) for slippage and flow
m.trade_tape.mechanism: The trade tape shows realized execution prices, aggressor side and size, giving slippage and informed-flow signals.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Large taker prints preceding a line move are a candidate informed-flow signal, and the tape sets realistic fill assumptions. Subtle: in thin NBA markets a single print can be a retail order, so it needs size and repeat-flow filters.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Per trade: price, size, taker side, timestamp; features: signed volume imbalance in trailing windows, VWAP vs mid, price impact of prints, time to next print.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

nba.stat_corrections.label: Post-game stat corrections and source-of-truth lag
nba.stat_corrections.mechanism: The settlement source can change after the game (scorer corrections to assists, rebounds, steals, minutes), which changes the realized label for razor-thin rungs.
nba.stat_corrections.rationale: Official NBA stat corrections occur within hours and sometimes days; a Kalshi settlement might use the figure at a defined time. Props sitting exactly at the line are exposed. Knowable pregame only as a historical base rate of corrections by stat type and arena, not for a given game.
nba.stat_corrections.measurement: From archived box scores at game end vs 24-48h later, compute correction frequency by stat and arena; read rules_text for source and settlement timing; flag rung-at-threshold exposure.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.market_calibration_bias.label: Price-bucket miscalibration (favorite-longshot, over bias) in NBA families
nba.market_calibration_bias.mechanism: Retail participation patterns can leave systematic bias by price level and direction (e.g. overs on star props) that shows up as a reliability-curve gap.
nba.market_calibration_bias.rationale: Distinct from fundamentals: a reliability curve per family and side tells how much to shade model probabilities toward or away from price. Highly regime-dependent and a pure hypothesis until tested on out-of-sample seasons. Must separate calibration at the rung level from game-level correlation.
nba.market_calibration_bias.measurement: Reliability curves (realized vs implied, 5c buckets) per family x side x main-line/alt-rung, using de-vigged book lines as the reference; calibration slope/intercept with game-clustered intervals.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

nba.implied_team_totals.label: Market-implied team points from spread and total
nba.implied_team_totals.mechanism: Spread and total jointly imply each team's expected points, which translate into possessions and efficiency for every player in that game.
nba.implied_team_totals.rationale: Team implied total = (total ± spread)/2. Player props (points, assists, rebounds, threes) scale with team points and with the game's pace, and the implied totals move on injury news before box-score features update. It is the compact summary of the book's view of pace and offense in this exact matchup with current availability.
nba.implied_team_totals.measurement: implied_home = (T - S)/2 and implied_away = (T + S)/2 where S is home spread (negative = home favorite); deviation from the team's season average points; movement since open.
free_sources: The Odds API (free tier, limited credits; sportsbook lines)
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.off_rtg.label: Opponent-adjusted offensive rating, lineup-adjusted
nba.off_rtg.mechanism: Points scored per 100 possessions, adjusted for opponent defense, venue and the current available roster, is the core of the expected scoring margin and total.
nba.off_rtg.rationale: Raw team ratings mix opponents and rosters; the relevant quantity is the rating of the lineup that will play tonight. Subtle: early-season and post-trade ratings are noisy and must be shrunk to a prior (preseason projection plus player-based estimate); recency weighting should favor games with the current core healthy; garbage-time possessions should be filtered.
nba.off_rtg.measurement: Ridge-regress game-level ORtg/DRtg on offense/defense/home dummies over a rolling window with exponential decay; filter garbage time (Cleaning-the-Glass-style rules from play-by-play); shrink toward preseason prior with weight growing with possessions; adjust for tonight's missing players using player on/off or RAPM values.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamdashboardbygeneralsplits / leaguedashteamstats
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.def_rtg.label: Opponent-adjusted defensive rating
nba.def_rtg.mechanism: Points allowed per 100 possessions adjusted for opponent offense and current roster determines how much the opponent's offense is suppressed.
nba.def_rtg.rationale: Defense is noisier than offense over short windows because opponent shooting luck (esp. opponent 3P% on open looks) is a large share of variation; ratings should be partly shrunk toward shot-quality-based expectation. Rim protector availability swings defensive rating more than any other single absence.
nba.def_rtg.measurement: Same ridge setup as offense on defensive rating; blend observed DRtg with expected DRtg from opponent shot quality allowed (location, openness); recency decay; adjust for tonight's absent rim protectors/wing stoppers via on/off.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.pace.label: Pace/possessions, opponent-adjusted, lineup-aware
nba.pace.mechanism: Possessions per game scale every counting stat and the total; the game's pace is a joint outcome of both teams' preferences and the lineups on the floor.
nba.pace.rationale: Pace is not additive: expected game pace is roughly league average plus each team's deviation, but slower teams usually win the tempo contest on defense and transition-heavy teams are constrained by opponent make-rates. Lineup changes (a primary ball-pusher out) shift pace. Blowouts and intentional fouling alter late possession counts.
nba.pace.measurement: Regress per-game possessions on team-offense and team-defense pace effects (or compute expected pace = league + (paceA - lg) + (paceB - lg)); filter to competitive minutes; lineup-adjust using on/off pace; compare to market implied total via possessions x efficiency.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.ratings.label: Team ratings / schedule strength for season markets
nba.ratings.mechanism: A season-level team rating (net rating plus roster talent plus health) feeds simulations for wins, seed, series and title.
nba.ratings.rationale: Season markets require a rating that combines prior-season performance, roster changes, current-season results and injury information; single-season net rating has meaningful luck variance. Subtle: ratings should reflect playoff-relevant strength (top-8 rotation health) rather than regular-season depth for title/series markets, and be uncertainty-aware.
nba.ratings.measurement: Bayesian team rating: preseason prior from player-based projection (minutes-weighted EPM/BPM/RAPM) updated by game results with margin capped and garbage filtered; produce mean and sd; separate regular-season and playoff rotation versions.
free_sources: DARKO (darko.app, free web view; no official API)
Dunks & Threes EPM (free partial; no official API)

nba.lineup_adj_rating.label: Availability-adjusted team rating for tonight's active set
nba.lineup_adj_rating.mechanism: Team strength given who is actually active, computed by summing player impact over expected minutes, moves spreads, totals and every player prop in the game.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.rationale: A star absence changes team net rating by an amount far larger than most other features; the market reprices within minutes of the report. The model needs an independent player-impact valuation to avoid just reading the market. Subtle: impact of replacing a player is not the star's full value (usage redistributes), and replacement is nonlinear when multiple players are out.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.measurement: Sum over expected-minute allocation of per-player impact (RAPM/EPM/BPM shrunk) for the active set vs team average-active baseline; difference gives point-spread adjustment; validate with with/without team splits when sample allows.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
DARKO (darko.app, free web view; no official API)
Dunks & Threes EPM (free partial; no official API)

nba.player_impact.label: Player impact value (RAPM/BPM/EPM-style) with shrinkage
nba.player_impact.mechanism: A shrunk player-level impact estimate converts availability changes into rating changes and anchors projections for newly acquired or returning players.
nba.player_impact.rationale: On/off splits alone are noisy; regularized adjusted plus-minus blended with box-score priors (BPM) gives more stable estimates. Used for lineup_adj_rating, awards and futures. Subtle: impact is context-dependent (lineup partners, role), aging, and minutes restrictions after injury.
nba.player_impact.measurement: Multi-year ridge RAPM with box-score prior, age curve and minutes-weighted shrinkage; separate offensive and defensive components; recency weighting of current season.
free_sources: DARKO (darko.app, free web view; no official API)
Dunks & Threes EPM (free partial; no official API)
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.venue.label: Arena/home-court effect
nba.venue.mechanism: Home court raises scoring margin through crowd, travel asymmetry, familiarity and referee behavior; the magnitude differs by arena and has changed over time.
nba.venue.rationale: League-wide NBA home advantage has been around 2-3 points but has varied and arena-specific effects (altitude, crowd) are small relative to noise, so team-specific home edges should be heavily shrunk. Neutral venues (Cup knockout, international games, Mexico City/Paris) need explicit treatment.
nba.venue.measurement: Estimate league home advantage per season by regression; team-specific deviation with strong shrinkage; flag neutral sites and international games.

nba.rest_travel.label: Rest, back-to-back, travel, altitude
nba.rest_travel.mechanism: Fatigue from short rest, back-to-backs and dense schedule modestly lowers efficiency and, through coaching decisions, changes minutes and availability.
nba.rest_travel.rationale: Rest effects on team performance are small but real; larger is the indirect channel where stars sit on the second night of a back-to-back, which is handled by availability inputs. Rest differential (not absolute rest) matters for the spread; 3-in-4 and 4-in-6 clusters, and games after long road trips, add tail risk. Subtle: effect sizes have shrunk in the sports-science era and must be fit on recent seasons only.
nba.rest_travel.measurement: Per team: days of rest, is_b2b, second_game_of_b2b_on_road, games in last 4/6/7 days, rest differential; interactions with age and minutes load; fit effect on margin residual vs closing line.

nba.travel_altitude.label: Travel distance, time zones, and altitude (Denver, Utah)
nba.travel_altitude.mechanism: Distance, time-zone change and high-altitude venues alter fatigue and shooting/endurance, mostly for visiting teams on short rest.
nba.travel_altitude.rationale: Altitude at Denver and Utah is the main environment effect hypothesized to matter in late-game fatigue; coast-to-coast trips with a day-game next stop are another. Effects likely small and can be absorbed by the market line, so mainly useful for second-order effects on totals and fourth-quarter minutes.
nba.travel_altitude.measurement: Great-circle distance since last game, time-zone shift, altitude of venue, interactions with is_b2b; evaluate residual vs line by period (late-game efficiency, Q4 scoring).

nba.standings_motivation.label: Standings, clinch/tank incentives and late-season motivation
nba.standings_motivation.mechanism: Teams out of contention or with locked seeds rest stars or play young players, changing availability and minutes distribution late in the season.
nba.standings_motivation.rationale: Late-season and post-clinch games show elevated load management and unpredictable rotations, making both sides and player props noisier and shifting minutes to bench players. Subtle: announcements arrive late (game-day), and tanking incentives (lottery odds) differ from effort incentives; play-in positioning and in-season Cup stakes alter incentives too.
nba.standings_motivation.measurement: Compute win-probability leverage per game from standings simulation (seed distribution sensitivity), clinch/elimination flags, games remaining, lottery odds sensitivity; interact with star age/injury history.

nba.referee_crew.label: Referee crew tendencies (fouls, pace, total, home bias)
nba.referee_crew.mechanism: The assigned crew's foul-calling rate sets free-throw volume, foul trouble, and game pace, affecting totals and certain player props.
nba.referee_crew.rationale: Crew assignments are public the morning of game day, so they are knowable but the effect is modest and the historical estimate noisy; crews with higher foul rates raise free-throw attempts and lower fluidity. Subtle: crew effects are partly confounded by the teams they officiated; need to regress crew effect on fouls/total residual controlling for teams.
nba.referee_crew.measurement: Mixed-effects model: total or FTA residual ~ crew chief + referees + team effects with shrinkage; rolling 2-3 seasons; compute expected fouls/FTA shift for tonight's crew.
free_sources: NBA official referee assignments (official.nba.com, free, posted morning of game day)
NBA Last Two Minute reports (official.nba.com, free)
Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) game box scores list officials

nba.fouls_ft.label: Foul drawing, free-throw rate and officials/referee crew
nba.fouls_ft.mechanism: Team and player foul-drawing rates and opponent foul-committing rates determine free-throw volume, an efficient scoring source that influences points and total.
nba.fouls_ft.rationale: FT rate is more stable than FT% and differs strongly by player role (rim attackers, bigs). Opponent foul rate allowed matters but is scheme-dependent (drop vs switching). Crew effect (see referee_crew) interacts. Subtle: FT attempts counted in totals but also lengthen games, and intentional fouling late skews FTA in blowouts/close games.
nba.fouls_ft.measurement: FTA per 100 possessions and per player-FGA for offense; opponent FTA allowed per 100; opponent-adjusted by regression; exclude intentional-foul possessions in last 2 minutes when estimating organic rate.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashplayerstats/teamstats (FTA, PFD)

nba.def_scheme.label: Team defensive scheme and play-type profile (drop, switch, blitz, zone)
nba.def_scheme.mechanism: Scheme determines which shots and passes are conceded, shaping opponent guard assists, big-man rebounds/scoring and three-point volume.
nba.def_scheme.rationale: Pick-and-roll coverage and switch rate change shot distribution: drop coverage concedes mid-range/pull-ups but protects the rim; switching reduces assists but can concede post mismatches and offensive rebounds. Scheme is multi-year-stable for most coaches, and lets us explain why a team allows high assist or rebound counts to a position.
nba.def_scheme.measurement: Play-type frequency and efficiency allowed (Synergy-like categories from NBA play-type endpoints), PnR ball-handler/roll-man ppp allowed, switch frequency from tracking/matchup data, opponent 3PA/rim FGA allowed rates, rank vs league; stability across seasons.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) synergyplaytypes, leaguedashptdefend
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.three_pt_luck.label: Team three-point shooting luck vs shot quality (own and opponent)
nba.three_pt_luck.mechanism: Realized team 3P% regresses toward a shot-quality-based expectation; opponent 3P% allowed is mostly outside the defense's control on open looks.
nba.three_pt_luck.rationale: Hot or cold shooting streaks inflate or deflate recent offensive/defensive ratings and totals; ignoring regression overstates how hot teams will score and how stingy lucky defenses are. Subtle: shooters' true skill still differs, so expectation must use shooter-specific priors and shot openness, not a league mean.
nba.three_pt_luck.measurement: Expected 3P% = sum over attempts of shooter prior (career/regressed) adjusted for openness; luck = actual - expected over trailing N games; estimate shrinkage factor from out-of-sample reversion; same for opponent 3P% allowed with league-mean prior weighted heavily.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) shotchartdetail, leaguedashteamshotlocations; synergy
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.pythag_residual.label: Point-differential vs record luck (Pythagorean residual, clutch record)
nba.pythag_residual.mechanism: Wins above point-differential expectation (close-game results) mean-revert, so records overstate or understate true strength for futures and win totals.
nba.pythag_residual.rationale: Records built on unusual clutch/close-game results are less predictive than margin-based ratings. Used mainly for season wins, seeds and playoff futures; also reveals when a market anchored to the standings misprices the true team. Subtle: coaching/late-game execution may have a small persistent component, so shrink rather than zero it out.
nba.pythag_residual.measurement: Pythagorean wins with exponent ~14 (fit by season) minus actual; clutch (score within 5, last 5 min) record vs expectation; apply 50% or fitted regression to remaining games.

nba.score_resid.label: Score residual distribution around lines
nba.score_resid.mechanism: The distribution of actual margin/total minus the closing line gives the variance, skew and tail mass needed to convert a point-spread/total edge into a probability.
nba.score_resid.rationale: NBA margin sd around the closing spread is roughly 11-12 points and total sd roughly 17-19; these differ by spread size (blowouts have fatter tails), pace and period. Subtle: the center of the residual distribution is zero if lines are efficient, so the use is the shape (variance by line size, push masses at integer numbers) rather than bias.
nba.score_resid.measurement: Compute empirical residual distribution of (margin + spread) and (total points - total) over multiple seasons by spread bucket and total bucket; fit scale; compute probability mass at integers for push/at-threshold handling.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) game logs
The Odds API (free tier, limited credits; sportsbook lines)
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.garbage.label: Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread
nba.garbage.mechanism: The probability and timing of a lopsided margin determine starter minutes loss, bench usage, and distortions to late scoring and period totals.
nba.garbage.rationale: Large pregame spreads and in-game leads cut starters' minutes (stars often finish 4-8 minutes below expectation in blowouts), reducing counting stats; this is the main reason high spreads depress over rates on star props. Subtle: effect depends on coach and on how early margin hits 20+; the distribution of minutes conditional on margin is non-linear.
nba.garbage.measurement: Estimate P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as function of closing spread from historical sims or empirical data; combine with coach-specific starter-pull thresholds; output expected starter-minute reduction.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay

nba.ot_model.label: Overtime probability and minutes
nba.ot_model.mechanism: Regulation ties send games to overtime (about 5-6% of games), adding about 5 minutes and typically ~10-12 points to totals and some player stats.
nba.ot_model.rationale: OT probability rises for tight spreads and low-scoring, slow games, and matters for markets that include OT in settlement (totals, spreads, player props) versus those that exclude it (period markets, some race-to markets). Subtle: probability is nearly flat across spreads under ±6, so the key is wording, not a precise model.
nba.ot_model.measurement: Empirical P(OT) by |spread| bucket and total bucket over multiple seasons; expected extra points per team per OT; adjust totals/player minutes if rules_text includes OT.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.late_game_script.label: Late-game foul and clock-management script
nba.late_game_script.mechanism: In close games the trailing team fouls intentionally and the leader attempts free throws, which inflate totals and free-throw counts; in blowouts clocks run out.
nba.late_game_script.rationale: This creates asymmetry between spreads/totals covers (a late garbage-time basket can flip a cover) and affects period-4 markets and FT props. Subtle: teams' propensity to foul when down 3-6 and stars' FT% on the leading team differ; coaches differ on when to start fouling.
nba.late_game_script.measurement: From play-by-play, rates of intentional fouls by score state, points scored in last 2 minutes by margin state, FT% of top-4 ball handlers on leading team; empirical cover-flip frequency as function of spread.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.injuries_pit.label: Injury report (official + ESPN) vintages, status changes
nba.injuries_pit.mechanism: Player status (out, doubtful, questionable, probable) as of a timestamp determines who plays, and hence minutes, usage and team strength.
nba.injuries_pit.rationale: The official report is posted in waves (afternoon the day before, updates through game day) and final inactives appear ~30-90 minutes before tip, so at a given decision time status is often only partially resolved. Status labels are not calibrated probabilities: 'questionable' resolves differently by team, player age, injury type and back-to-back. Subtle: the report vintage (not the final inactive list) is the legitimate pregame feature.
nba.injuries_pit.measurement: Archive every report snapshot with retrieved_at; per player: status, reason text, time of last change, number of status flips; feature as-of decision time; link to final actual availability only as a label.
free_sources: NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.status_resolution_prob.label: Probability a questionable/GTD player plays (calibrated)
nba.status_resolution_prob.mechanism: A calibrated play probability for uncertain statuses converts a discrete report label into expected minutes and a mixture over scenarios.
nba.status_resolution_prob.rationale: Using 'questionable' as a coin flip loses information: historical play rates depend on injury body part, whether the player practiced, team, rest day, stakes, and whether the player was already ruled 'probable' earlier. Mixture-modeling over play/no-play for key teammates changes every prop in the game. Subtle: the resolution event (inactive list) can arrive after the market closes, so the stake sizing must be unconditional on it.
nba.status_resolution_prob.measurement: Fit calibrated classifier on historical (status, injury type, minutes since report, back-to-back, home/away, team) -> played; expected-value projection = p * E[X | plays, restrictions] + (1-p) * (teammate scenario).
free_sources: NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)
Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) box scores (DNP reason)

nba.starters_pit.label: Starting lineups / confirmed starters timestamped
nba.starters_pit.mechanism: The starting five determines opening-quarter rotations, minute allocation, first-basket and first-quarter markets, and often signals the intended minutes plan.
nba.starters_pit.rationale: Starters are confirmed only ~30 minutes before tip, although projected starters are available earlier and a coach's pattern rarely changes without an injury. Starter status differs from minutes: a bench sixth man can play more than a starter. Subtle: a non-obvious starter change (rest, matchup-based) is informative about the minutes plan and should be captured with source timestamp.
nba.starters_pit.measurement: Archive projected and confirmed starters with timestamps; compute probability of starting from recent patterns, injuries and coach history; features: confirmed changes vs most common lineup.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) boxscore starters (post-hoc); ESPN game summary
NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)
Rotowire/FantasyLabs public lineup pages (free web view; no API)

nba.load_mgmt.label: Load management / return-from-injury minutes restrictions
nba.load_mgmt.mechanism: Teams rest stars on back-to-backs, in lopsided situations and when returning from injury with announced minute limits, reducing minutes unpredictably.
nba.load_mgmt.rationale: Load management is a policy: age, injury history, rest rules (e.g. no consecutive-night games for certain players), and clinching status predict absences and minute caps. Returning players typically have restrictions (e.g. 20-24 minutes) that are first announced or reported on game day, so a pregame model must carry a probability. Subtle: the NBA's player participation policies and 65-game award eligibility alter incentives.
nba.load_mgmt.measurement: Player-level: games missed on back-to-backs vs non-b2b, age, prior-season availability, injury return flags, games since return, restrictions reported; team-level policy tendency; probability of rest by day-of-week and rest status.
free_sources: NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)
Spotrac / RealGM / Pro Sports Transactions (free tiers: contracts, cap, transactions)

nba.news.label: Transactions, trades, coaching news
nba.news.mechanism: Roster moves and coaching changes alter minutes allocation, team strength and future markets.
nba.news.rationale: Trades, signings, buyouts, two-way conversions and coach changes change roles with a lag; a newly acquired player has uncertain minutes, a new coach changes pace and rotation. News also drives off-court event markets and season futures. Subtle: timestamps and source reliability matter; rumors precede transactions.
nba.news.measurement: Time-stamped feed of transactions; derived features: days since trade, new-coach flag, rookies/two-way call-ups, teammate-absence from trades; event-arrival base rates.
free_sources: Spotrac / RealGM / Pro Sports Transactions (free tiers: contracts, cap, transactions)

nba.minutes.label: Projected minutes (role, blowout risk, foul trouble)
nba.minutes.mechanism: Minutes are the largest single driver of every counting stat; the distribution of minutes (not the mean) governs the tails of over/under markets.
nba.minutes.rationale: Minutes projections must combine recent role, coach rotation, teammates available, opponent matchup, back-to-back, and the spread-based blowout probability. A star averaging 34 minutes may have a 25% chance of <30 in a blowout. Realized minutes are not knowable pregame; only the distribution. Subtle: using season-average minutes without conditioning on availability of teammates overstates minutes when the depth chart is full and understates when key players are out.
nba.minutes.measurement: Regression/quantile model of minutes on: trailing minutes (EWMA), starter flag, days rest, teammates out (counts weighted by their minutes), spread, team pace, coach; output mean and full distribution (mixture with blowout and foul-trouble branches).
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) playergamelogs / boxscoretraditional
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.rotation.label: Rotation patterns, minutes distribution by lineup/scoreboard margin
nba.rotation.mechanism: How a coach distributes minutes across lineups, quarters and score margins determines starter rest patterns, bench usage and period-level scoring.
nba.rotation.rationale: Coaches use predictable substitution patterns (starters' first stint ~6-9 minutes, rest in Q2, closing lineup in Q4) that change with injuries and margin. These patterns drive quarter markets, first-half markets and star minutes. Subtle: patterns shift after trades or lineup experiments; the distribution of minutes by margin bin is what matters for blowout adjustment.
nba.rotation.measurement: From play-by-play stints: stint lengths, first sub time, minutes by quarter, by score margin bin (|margin| 0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20+), starter minutes lost when team up/down 20; coach-level pooled priors.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.starter_probability.label: Probability a player starts / closes (role-change estimate)
nba.starter_probability.mechanism: A player's start/close status and bench-to-starter swaps determine role and minute allocation and are triggered by teammate absence.
nba.starter_probability.rationale: When a starter is out the coach elevates a specific replacement (often the next big or the best guard), and that replacement's volume jumps; which replacement depends on position needs and coach habits, observable in past absence games. Prices on player props often lag the replacement identification until inactives are confirmed.
nba.starter_probability.measurement: From past games with a given starter absent: who replaced them and with what minutes/usage; coach-specific replacement mapping; probability = share of past absences where player A was the replacement.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits) lineup stats

nba.teammate_absence_shift.label: With/without teammate splits: usage, minutes and stat redistribution
nba.teammate_absence_shift.mechanism: When key teammates are out, shot attempts, ball-handling, and rebound opportunities redistribute to the remaining players in a structured way (not evenly).
nba.teammate_absence_shift.rationale: This is the largest edge source for props: a lead guard out raises the backup guard's usage and assists, but a primary scorer out lowers assists for his passing partner (fewer converted passes). Direction depends on whether the absent player consumes the stat (usage, rebounds) or produces teammates' stat conversion (shooters). Subtle: with/without samples are small and confounded by opponent and by injuries to multiple players; use hierarchical shrinkage and role-based priors.
nba.teammate_absence_shift.measurement: Per player: stat per minute and minutes with teammate X on/off the roster, over games where X missed; hierarchical shrinkage to a role-based redistribution model (usage, ball handling, rebound share absorbed); evaluate for combinations of absences.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.usage.label: Usage rate, shot attempts, creation share
nba.usage.mechanism: The share of team possessions a player ends (shots, FT trips, turnovers) determines their scoring attempts and, via creation role, assist and turnover rates.
nba.usage.rationale: Usage is relatively stable per player but increases when teammates sit and decreases in lineups with other high-usage players. Efficiency and usage trade off; points per minute depends on both. Subtle: usage computed from season averages misses lineup-specific usage, and on/off-lineup splits are small.
nba.usage.measurement: USG% and FGA/FTA/TOV per 36 minutes with exponentially weighted recency; lineup-conditional usage; creation share = (FGA + 0.44 FTA + TOV + potential assists)/team possessions while on court.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.touches.label: Touches, time of possession, ball-handling load
nba.touches.mechanism: Touches and time of possession measure how often the player has the ball, a prerequisite for assists, turnovers and shot creation.
nba.touches.rationale: High touch/time-of-possession players generate passes and potential assists independent of whether teammates convert; touches are more stable than assists. Subtle: touch counts differ by arena tracking and by role (bigs with high touches in the high post vs guards in transition).
nba.touches.measurement: Per 36 minutes: touches, front-court touches, time of possession, passes made, average seconds per touch, drives; lineup splits when other ball handlers are out.

nba.pot_ast.label: Potential assists, passes, secondary assists
nba.pot_ast.mechanism: Potential assists (passes that lead to a shot attempt) are the opportunity count; actual assists are potential assists times teammate make probability.
nba.pot_ast.rationale: Decomposing assists into opportunities and conversion separates stable creation from noisy teammate shot-making. Potential assists per minute are more persistent than assists, and shift predictably with teammates' availability and pace. Subtle: assist credit also depends on official scorer tendencies and on what counts as 'assisted' (dunks, rim shots), and 3P assists are worth more points but not more assists.
nba.pot_ast.measurement: Potential assists per 36 and per touch, secondary and free-throw assists, assisted-FG share of teammates; EWMA recency; adjust for opponent pace and teammates on court via lineup shares.

nba.teammate_conv.label: Teammate shot conversion / shooting quality
nba.teammate_conv.mechanism: Assists depend on whether the shots a player creates are made; the shooting skill and shot quality of teammates on the floor raises or lowers conversion.
nba.teammate_conv.rationale: Teammate expected eFG on the passes created (shooters like catch-and-shoot specialists vs low-percentage players) changes assists per potential assist from ~0.4 to ~0.6. Subtle: conversion has luck (hot/cold shooters) that should be regressed, but real roster quality changes (star shooter returning or leaving) is real signal.
nba.teammate_conv.measurement: AST/potential assist history; expected conversion = sum over teammates of pass share x teammate expected eFG given shot type; use shrinkage; condition on which teammates are active tonight.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) shotchartdetail, leaguedashptstats (Passing: by teammate)
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.reb_chances.label: Rebound chances and contested rebounds
nba.reb_chances.mechanism: Rebounds are opportunity (chances) times conversion; chances depend on position on the floor, teammates' rebounding and the volume of missed shots.
nba.reb_chances.rationale: Rebound chances (a ball within reach) are more stable than rebounds themselves, and conversion depends on contest rate. The rebounding share of a lineup is zero-sum: a big out raises rebounds for remaining bigs and guards. Subtle: team-level rebound totals depend on both teams' misses and shot types (long 3PT rebounds go to guards/wings more).
nba.reb_chances.measurement: Per 36: rebound chances, contested/uncontested split, rebound conversion; lineup rebound share; condition on frontcourt teammates on floor; shrink conversion rates.

nba.rebound_pool.label: Rebound pool: expected missed shots in the game by type
nba.rebound_pool.mechanism: Total available rebounds equal both teams' missed field goals and free throws; pace and shooting efficiency determine the pool, and shot type changes where rebounds go.
nba.rebound_pool.rationale: A high-pace, low-efficiency game produces many missed shots and more rebounds per player. Pool depends on expected FGA and FG% for both teams (and the 3P share, because 3-point misses produce longer rebounds that favor guards). The market total and spread give implied pace/efficiency.
nba.rebound_pool.measurement: Pool = (FGA_a*(1-FG%_a) + FGA_b*(1-FG%_b)) + 0.44*FTA misses (last FT only); estimate from pace, team shot profile, and matchup; split by shot zone for rebound-location effects.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.frontcourt_competition.label: Frontcourt competition for boards (bigs on floor, lineup size)
nba.frontcourt_competition.mechanism: The identity and number of other rebounders on the floor (centers, forwards) and the opponent's offensive-rebounding size determine each player's share of board chances.
nba.frontcourt_competition.rationale: Rebounds are a share game: when two bigs share a lineup each gets fewer. Opponent size and offensive rebounding strategy (crash vs get back) shifts defensive rebound chances. Subtle: small-ball lineup usage depends on matchup and injuries and is only partially predictable pregame.
nba.frontcourt_competition.measurement: Share of team rebounds while on court with each frontcourt teammate; expected lineup frontcourt minutes; opponent ORB% and crash rate; model rebound share given lineup composition.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.player_role_position.label: Position/role classification (ball handler, wing, big, stretch)
nba.player_role_position.mechanism: Role determines which stats a player generates and which opponent weaknesses apply; positional labels are ambiguous in the modern NBA.
nba.player_role_position.rationale: Opponent-vs-position statistics depend on a meaningful position mapping. A tracking-based role (primary handler, spacer, roll man, post-up, rim protector) predicts who takes the stat opportunities better than listed position. Subtle: players change roles within seasons and teams (e.g., center playing guard-like roles).
nba.player_role_position.measurement: Cluster players on play-type frequencies, touches, shot zones, rebound share, passing; maintain role label per game based on lineup context; map to opponent allowed-by-role statistics.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) synergyplaytypes, leaguedashptstats

nba.opp_def_pos.label: Opponent defense vs position / stat allowed
nba.opp_def_pos.mechanism: The opponent's defense concedes different amounts of points, rebounds, assists, and threes to specific roles, depending on scheme and personnel.
nba.opp_def_pos.rationale: Opponent-allowed stats by position are noisy and heavily confounded by opponent strength and the specific players faced; they matter mostly where scheme is extreme (rim protection, switching, drop, pressure) and must be shrunk heavily. Subtle: 'allowed to position' can reflect which opponents the team has faced, so adjust for the opponents' own season averages (compare allowed vs opponent norm).
nba.opp_def_pos.measurement: For each stat: stat allowed to role-group per 100 possessions relative to those players' season averages (ratio-of-ratios), shrink to league mean by sample, recency decay; sample by stat type (assist rate, rebounds, 3PA).
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashplayerstats with opponent filters
Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) (team opponent splits)
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.opp_ast_allowed.label: Opponent assist-suppression profile (assists per made FG allowed by role, switching)
nba.opp_ast_allowed.mechanism: How often the opponent's made baskets are assisted (and by whom) reflects its scheme: switching and isolation-forcing defenses reduce passes, pressure forces turnovers.
nba.opp_ast_allowed.rationale: Assist ratio allowed per opponent FGM varies by scheme and personnel; a team facing a heavy-switching defense produces more isolation and fewer assisted baskets. The effect is on the share of FGM assisted and on potential assists. Subtle: requires separate treatment of assist rate and shot volume, otherwise high-pace teams look like high-assist teams.
nba.opp_ast_allowed.measurement: Opponent AST/FGM allowed, potential assists allowed per possession, share of assisted threes vs rim shots allowed, switch rate; opponent-adjust by regressing on the offense's own AST/FGM; use ratios not counts.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamdashboardbygeneralsplits (Opponent), leaguedashptstats
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.matchup_def.label: Individual defensive matchup / scheme (drop, switch)
nba.matchup_def.mechanism: The primary defender's skill and size and the coverage on the player's pick-and-roll change shot quality, points and passing options.
nba.matchup_def.rationale: A scorer facing an elite on-ball defender or a rim-protecting big sees changes in shot mix; matchups are not published pregame and change by lineup. Subtle: matchup data is sparse, and usage is mostly fixed by role, so effect sizes are small except for very strong or weak defenders.
nba.matchup_def.measurement: From matchup tracking, points per possession allowed when guarded by each defender and shot quality; expected defender assignment by position/starter; effect = guarded-by-A differences shrunk to league.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leagueseasonmatchups, matchupsrollup
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.shot_profile.label: Shot location/profile (rim/mid/3), zone defense allowed
nba.shot_profile.mechanism: A team's or player's distribution of attempts by zone and the opponent's zone defense determine expected efficiency and the mix of points, rebounds and threes.
nba.shot_profile.rationale: Expected points per shot depends on shot zone, and defenses concede zones in a stable way (drop teams give mid-range, switching gives threes). For props it sets 3PA and rim-attack volume; for totals it sets efficiency. Subtle: opponent adjustment requires matching offense zone frequency with defense zone frequency allowed (not simply averaging).
nba.shot_profile.measurement: Zone frequencies and FG% by zone for offense and defense (restricted area, paint, mid, corner 3, above-break 3); expected points per attempt using matchup-weighted frequencies; shrink FG% by zone to league mean.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) shotchartdetail, leaguedashteamshotlocations
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.three_volume.label: 3PA rate, catch-and-shoot share, 3P% shrinkage and opponent 3PA allowed
nba.three_volume.mechanism: Threes made equal attempts times make probability; attempts are driven by role, minutes and opponent scheme, and make% must be shrunk heavily.
nba.three_volume.rationale: A player's 3PA per minute is much more stable than 3P%; make% over a season reverts toward career and shot-quality-based expectation. Opponent 3PA allowed and pace/spacing change attempt volume. Subtle: attempts are overdispersed (game-to-game volume varies), so a binomial with fixed attempts understates variance.
nba.three_volume.measurement: 3PA per 36 (EWMA), catch-and-shoot vs pull-up share, shot openness; 3P% shrunk with beta prior (career/team) with prior weight about 200-300 attempts; opponent 3PA allowed per 100 relative to league; negative-binomial attempts model.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashplayerptshot / shotchartdetail
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.player_shooting_regression.label: Player shooting luck vs expectation (3P%, FG%, FT%)
nba.player_shooting_regression.mechanism: Hot or cold stretches in 3P%/FG%/FT% mostly regress to a player's shot-quality-adjusted talent, so recent form overstates the next game's expected efficiency.
nba.player_shooting_regression.rationale: Markets and naive models overweight recent hot shooting; true talent is better estimated by priors from career, volume and shot openness. FT% stabilizes faster than 3P%. Subtle: real changes (mechanics, injury recovery, role) exist, so shrinkage weight should depend on sample size and change signals.
nba.player_shooting_regression.measurement: Beta-binomial shrinkage with prior mean = career/role expectation and prior strength set empirically per stat (3P ~ 300-500 att, FT ~ 100-150 att); compare recent vs shrunk estimate; include shot-quality (openness) adjustment.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.steal_block_rates.label: Steals/blocks per minute, opponent turnover and rim-attempt rates
nba.steal_block_rates.mechanism: Steals and blocks are low-count events driven by per-minute skill, minutes, and the opponent's turnover and rim-attempt propensities.
nba.steal_block_rates.rationale: Per-minute rates are fairly stable for steals/blocks, and opponent turnover rate (esp. live-ball turnovers) and rim attempts per possession modulate them. Their low-count Poisson nature means strike lines at 0.5 and 1.5 are dominated by dispersion modeling. Subtle: official-scorer credit (esp. blocks and steals) varies by arena.
nba.steal_block_rates.measurement: Per-36 steals/blocks (EWMA, shrink with Gamma-Poisson prior), opponent TOV% and live-ball TOV per 100, opponent rim FGA per 100, matchup-adjusted; minutes distribution to produce count distribution.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashplayerstats, hustlestats

nba.turnover_pressure.label: Turnover propensity and opponent pressure (turnovers per touch, deflections)
nba.turnover_pressure.mechanism: Turnovers scale with ball-handling load and are raised by opponent pressure, deflections and steal rates.
nba.turnover_pressure.rationale: Turnover props depend on usage/ball handling as well as opponent live-ball pressure; high-assist creators also turn the ball over more. Subtle: turnover counts correlate with assists and minutes, so independent modeling misprices combos and conditional stats; scorer judgments (bad pass vs lost ball) are noisy.
nba.turnover_pressure.measurement: TOV per 100 touches/possessions used, bad-pass vs lost-ball split; opponent forced TOV% and deflections per 100; ball-handler pressure ratio; negative binomial with minutes.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) hustlestats, leaguedashptstats

nba.ft_attempts.label: Free-throw attempt rate and FT% (for FT-made props), opponent foul-rate allowed
nba.ft_attempts.mechanism: Free throws made equal attempts (drives, post play, foul-drawing, and late-game fouling) times FT%.
nba.ft_attempts.rationale: FTA/FGA is a stable per-player trait; FT% has a high true-talent component but moderate sampling noise. Late-game intentional fouls raise attempts for the leading team's ball handlers and make FT props sensitive to game script. Subtle: FT made props at 0.5/1.5/2.5 depend heavily on minutes and referees; overdispersed.
nba.ft_attempts.measurement: FTA per 36 and per FGA (EWMA), FT% shrunk with Beta prior; opponent FTA allowed per 100 relative to league; crew foul index; game script factor for last-2-minute fouling.

nba.foul_rates.label: Personal fouls per minute, foul-out and foul-trouble minute loss
nba.foul_rates.mechanism: Players with high foul rates face early-foul benching and foul-outs that cut minutes and counting stats, especially bigs against foul-drawing offenses.
nba.foul_rates.rationale: Foul trouble truncates minutes non-linearly and produces left-tail outcomes in over/under props; it is predictable in terms of baseline (PF per 36) and opponent (drawn fouls, big-vs-big matchups) but not realized. Subtle: coaches differ in how early they bench players with 2 fouls in the first half; crew effect interacts.
nba.foul_rates.measurement: PF per 36, P(2 fouls in Q1/first half) and P(foul-out) from game logs; minutes lost distribution in foul-trouble games; opponent drawn-foul rate; crew foul index; coach rule for early fouls.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay

nba.scorer_bias.label: Official scorer/arena stat-credit bias (assists, steals, blocks, rebounds)
nba.scorer_bias.mechanism: Statistics like assists, blocks and steals are subjective official-scorer judgments, and arena-level tendencies (home scorer) can shift counts systematically.
nba.scorer_bias.rationale: If home arenas credit more assists/blocks/steals to the home team, prop outcomes depend on venue and the scorer culture; the effect can be measured as arena-level residual in stat/min controlling for team and opponent. It is a hypothesis, probably small, and needs panel data over multiple seasons. Subtle: team-composition confounds (a team always plays at its own arena), so use opponent-team residuals at the same venue.
nba.scorer_bias.measurement: Mixed-effects model of assists/blocks/steals per 100 possessions with team-offense, team-defense and venue random effects; arena effect = home-arena random effect on both teams.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) team game logs by arena
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.tip_first_shot.label: Tip-off winner tendencies and first-shot/first-basket usage
nba.tip_first_shot.mechanism: The tip winner and opening play design determine who takes the first shot, and with starters fixed, first-shot share dominates first-basket probability.
nba.tip_first_shot.rationale: First-basket markets depend on tip winner probability (center vertical, ~50/50 with small edges), team's opening set plays (who the first shot is designed for), and shooter conversion on the first attempt. Subtle: very low base rates mean even small modeling errors matter; opening play patterns change after injuries/new starters.
nba.tip_first_shot.measurement: From play-by-play: first possession shot-taker distribution by starter lineup, jump-ball winner rates by center matchup, opening-play type (ATO), first FGA/first FGM share per player; EWMA with lineup conditioning.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.first_basket_share.label: First-basket history by team and player (first FGM share, first possession usage)
nba.first_basket_share.mechanism: The share of games where a player scores the team's first basket reflects set-play design and usage on the opening possessions.
nba.first_basket_share.rationale: Opening possessions differ from average possessions (set plays for specific scorers, centers off tip). Rates are small and sample-limited; they must be shrunk to usage-based priors. Also depends on which team scores first, linking to tip and defense. Subtle: starter changes reshape the distribution.
nba.first_basket_share.measurement: Per player: P(first team basket) and P(first game basket) from last 1-2 seasons, shrunk toward usage-share prior; condition on lineup identity; combine with P(team scores first) and P(tip).
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.q_scoring.label: Historical scoring by quarter/half, first-quarter pace and starter minutes
nba.q_scoring.mechanism: Period totals/margins depend on starter minutes in that period, pace and efficiency conditional on lineup, and game state in later periods.
nba.q_scoring.rationale: Q1 is dominated by starters (lineups known pregame), Q2 mixes benches and Q4 is state-dependent (garbage time, close-game fouls). First-half share of game total differs by team (slow starters, halftime adjustments). Subtle: period totals have higher relative variance than game totals and key lattice effects.
nba.q_scoring.measurement: Per team: points scored/allowed by quarter and half, adjusted for opponent and lineup; first-half share of game points; variance by period; calibrate to period lines vs actual.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamdashboard by period (boxscoretraditional by period)
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.bench_scoring.label: Bench scoring share and rotation depth by team
nba.bench_scoring.mechanism: Bench points depend on how many players the coach plays, the quality of reserves and the starters' minutes load.
nba.bench_scoring.rationale: Bench points markets/tie-ins depend on injuries to starters (promotes bench players into starter role and reduces the 'bench' denominator), blowout minutes, and rotation depth. Subtle: definition of bench is 'did not start', so lineup changes alter the market outcome mechanically.
nba.bench_scoring.measurement: Team bench points per game by opponent/spread bucket, rotation depth (players over 10 minutes), starters' minute shares; adjust for who starts tonight.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamdashboardbygeneralsplits (starters vs bench)

nba.stat_dist.label: Per-stat count distributions (overdispersion, correlation)
nba.stat_dist.mechanism: Player stat counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because minutes, role and game state vary; the correct distribution shape determines tail probabilities across rungs.
nba.stat_dist.rationale: Over/under probabilities at a line require the whole distribution: minutes mixture, negative binomial or zero-inflated forms, and ceiling/floor effects (blowout minutes). Stat correlations within a game (pts, ast, tov) matter for combos. Subtle: fitting only a mean from a line and a normal sd mis-prices tails at 25+, 30+ rungs.
nba.stat_dist.measurement: Fit count models (NB, mixtures over minutes scenarios) per player-stat with covariates; check dispersion, rung calibration; estimate correlation matrix of stats given minutes.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) game logs
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.combo_covariance.label: Covariance between stat components in combos (PRA, PR, PA, RA)
nba.combo_covariance.mechanism: Combined-stat markets sum correlated components: minutes create positive covariance, while role tradeoffs and game scripts can create negative covariance.
nba.combo_covariance.rationale: Variance of PRA is not the sum of component variances; positive correlation via minutes widens the tails, while negative correlation (usage vs assist focus) narrows them. Market makers often price combos from component lines, leaving mismatches. Subtle: covariance depends on role (center vs guard) and game script.
nba.combo_covariance.measurement: Estimate within-game covariance matrix (pts, reb, ast) per player conditional on minutes; simulate joint outcomes; compare implied combo distribution with sum of marginal rungs.
free_sources: hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.milestone_rates.label: Double-double/triple-double base rates and threshold proximity
nba.milestone_rates.mechanism: DD/TD are binary conjunctions of several count thresholds, so their probability depends on the joint distribution and proximity of each component to 10.
nba.milestone_rates.rationale: A player whose average assists are 7 and rebounds 11 has a double-double probability that is a product-like function of both stats' distribution; triple doubles are rare and depend on minutes and teammate shot-making. Subtle: coaches and scripts (blowouts) cut the tail; stat-padding behavior in last minutes is plausible but small.
nba.milestone_rates.measurement: Joint simulation from stat distributions per player, calibrated against historical DD/TD rates by minute bucket and third-stat distribution; compute P(any 2 of 3 >= 10).
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) game logs/DD-TD logs

nba.tracking.label: Tracking data (speed, defender distance, rim protection)
nba.tracking.mechanism: Tracking-derived measures (shot defender distance, rim deterrence, speed, drives) describe shot quality and defensive impact beyond box scores.
nba.tracking.rationale: Contested-vs-open breakdowns separate shooting skill from shot quality and expose rim-protection differences that box scores miss. Public access is partial and endpoints are rate-limited; many fine-grained tracking fields are only available as aggregates. Subtle: tracking-based tags change definitions over seasons, so historical comparability needs checking.
nba.tracking.measurement: Aggregate: shots by defender distance and zone, rim-defense DFG% at the rim, drives per game, speed/distance, hustle stats; use as shrunk, opponent-adjusted covariates into shot-quality and rebound models.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashptstats, leaguedashptdefend, leaguehustlestatsplayer
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.onoff.label: On/off and lineup combination efficiency
nba.onoff.mechanism: Lineup- and player-level on/off efficiency estimates the effect of specific absences/combos on team ratings, usually after shrinkage.
nba.onoff.rationale: On/off is the raw material for availability-adjusted ratings and lineup adjustments but is noisy and confounded by teammates and opponent quality; combinations of 5-man units have tiny samples. Subtle: use regularized estimates (RAPM) and only trust combos with large minutes.
nba.onoff.measurement: On/off net rating with opponent adjustments and shrinkage; lineup-level net ratings with minutes threshold; with/without splits for key teammates.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamplayeronoffdetails, teamdashlineups
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.standings_sim.label: Season/playoff simulation, tiebreakers, play-in
nba.standings_sim.mechanism: A Monte Carlo of the remaining schedule using team ratings, injuries and tiebreakers produces probabilities for seeds, playoffs, play-in, divisions and conference outcomes.
nba.standings_sim.rationale: Season futures are determined by the full distribution of outcomes including tiebreaker rules (head-to-head, division record, conference record), the play-in tournament and the Cup effect on the schedule; simple win-total extrapolation misses boundary effects near seed lines. Subtle: rating uncertainty must be sampled across sims, not fixed, otherwise tails are overconfident.
nba.standings_sim.measurement: Simulate remaining games from team ratings with home advantage, rest, and injury scenarios; sample rating uncertainty; implement official tiebreaker order and play-in bracket; output seed pmf and series probabilities.

nba.award_stats.label: Award-candidate production, voting narrative
nba.award_stats.mechanism: Award outcomes depend on production, team success, availability and media narrative; the voting process itself (ballot structure) shapes outcomes.
nba.award_stats.rationale: Historical voters favor high-volume scoring or advanced metrics depending on award, team seed and games played; modeling voting shares requires features like PER/BPM/win shares, team record, games played, narrative and rank in ballots. Subtle: the 65-game eligibility minimum and late-season injuries heavily alter finalists.
nba.award_stats.measurement: Per candidate: per-game stats, BPM/VORP/win shares, team win%, games played, minutes; historical vote-share regression by award; narrative proxies (odds, media consensus).
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) award voting history and advanced stats

nba.games_played_eligibility.label: Award/ranking eligibility rules (65-game minimum, minutes/stat thresholds)
nba.games_played_eligibility.mechanism: Eligibility thresholds convert missed games into a hard cutoff that determines whether a player can win or make an All-NBA team.
nba.games_played_eligibility.rationale: A candidate on pace to miss the games threshold has a lower probability of award or selection regardless of production; teams may manage minutes to preserve eligibility or fail. Rules have specific exceptions (partial games, appeals) and changes between seasons, which must be read from official rules text.
nba.games_played_eligibility.measurement: Track games played and games remaining vs threshold; compute probability of meeting threshold using injury risk; encode rule exceptions; flag borderline candidates.
free_sources: NBA official award eligibility rules (nba.com/official, free)

nba.voting_narrative.label: Media narrative, voter composition and ballot dynamics
nba.voting_narrative.mechanism: Voting for awards and selections reflects narrative (momentum, team success, positional balance) and ballot structure, not only statistics.
nba.voting_narrative.rationale: Narrative signals can be partly measured from betting market prices, media rankings, and award-tracker ladders; position constraints in All-NBA balloting (guard/forward/center) affect selection. Subtle: narrative-based features have small samples and are prone to overfit.
nba.voting_narrative.measurement: Ladder-ranking data (media award trackers), position-balloting rules, historical gaps between production rank and voting rank; use ordinal logit by award.
free_sources: ESPN/other media award trackers (free articles; no API)

nba.title_path.label: Playoff bracket path, matchup and home-court structure
nba.title_path.mechanism: Series winner and title probabilities depend on the bracket path (seed, opponent strength, home-court) and matchup-specific adjustments.
nba.title_path.rationale: Title odds are the product of series-win probabilities along a path that depends on which seed you are, who you face and the rest/injury states. A given team's path difficulty can differ substantially even for equal rating. Subtle: series outcomes are correlated through injuries to key players across rounds.
nba.title_path.measurement: Simulate bracket with seed distribution and series-level win probability; incorporate matchup tweaks (style, pace, rim protection) and home-court structure (2-2-1-1-1).

nba.series_model.label: Best-of-seven series model (home-court, game-to-game correlation, adjustments)
nba.series_model.mechanism: Series win and game-count probabilities derive from per-game win probabilities with home pattern; correlated injuries and adjustments change the distribution.
nba.series_model.rationale: A simple independent binomial overstates sweeps vs actual; playoff rotations shorten, pace slows, and stars play more minutes, shifting the effective team rating. Series props (sweep, exact games, player series totals) need game-level scoring simulations. Subtle: in-series injuries and coaching adjustments create positive correlation between games.
nba.series_model.measurement: Per-game win p from playoff-adjusted ratings with home advantage; sample game-to-game correlation parameter; adapt rating after injuries; compute pmf of series length and winner.

nba.playoff_rotation.label: Playoff rotation tightening and minutes inflation
nba.playoff_rotation.mechanism: Playoff games feature shorter rotations and higher starter minutes, changing player props and team-level ratings relative to the regular season.
nba.playoff_rotation.rationale: Stars play several more minutes per game and bench depth matters less; regular-season minutes baselines understate playoff volume for starters and overstate bench contributions. Subtle: the effect varies by round and by series pace/blowout probability.
nba.playoff_rotation.measurement: Compare each player's playoff vs regular-season minutes in historical series; team-level rotation depth; adjust minutes projections and series stat distributions by round.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.cup_format.label: NBA Cup group/knockout structure and tiebreakers
nba.cup_format.mechanism: Cup outcomes depend on group-stage point-differential tiebreakers, wildcard rules and single-elimination knockout games, with unusual incentives and neutral sites.
nba.cup_format.rationale: Group-stage point differential makes blowout margins matter in Cup games; rest decisions and star availability vary relative to regular-season games; the knockout games are neutral-site single games. Subtle: rules details change by season and the settlement rule for Cup counts must be read from official documentation.
nba.cup_format.measurement: Enumerate remaining group games with margin/tiebreaker simulation, apply wildcard rules, knockout bracket at neutral site; adjust for star minutes and motivation.

nba.sos_remaining.label: Remaining schedule strength and rest structure
nba.sos_remaining.mechanism: The strength, location and rest pattern of remaining opponents modulate expected wins, seeds and playoff probability.
nba.sos_remaining.rationale: Equal-rating teams with different remaining schedules have different expected finishes; back-to-back and road-heavy stretches affect both rating and injury risk. Subtle: strength must be measured with current availability-adjusted ratings, not preseason.
nba.sos_remaining.measurement: Sum expected win probabilities for remaining games with home, rest, and opponent availability-adjusted ratings; difference vs baseline schedule.

nba.injury_risk_season.label: Season-level availability risk (games missed expectations, injury history)
nba.injury_risk_season.mechanism: Expected games missed by key players changes season win totals, seed, awards and futures via lost minutes.
nba.injury_risk_season.rationale: Players with long injury histories, age and heavy minutes miss more games; season markets (wins, stat leaders, awards) are exposed. Subtle: injury events are rare/high-impact and fat-tailed; the model needs a mixture with a small probability of season-ending absence.
nba.injury_risk_season.measurement: Hazard model: games missed per season by age, position, prior injury, minutes; simulate availability; propagate through minutes to team rating and player stat totals.
free_sources: Spotrac / RealGM / Pro Sports Transactions (free tiers: contracts, cap, transactions) (injury/transactions history)
NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)

nba.season_stat_pace.label: Season-to-date pace and per-game stat trajectory for leaders
nba.season_stat_pace.mechanism: Season stat leader and streak markets depend on current totals, per-game rates, minutes and games remaining, with variance from injuries.
nba.season_stat_pace.rationale: A leader market is a race between players' cumulative totals; the gap and rate difference with remaining games define probability, with injury/rest scenarios central. Subtle: per-game average leaderboards have minimum games rules that interact with load management.
nba.season_stat_pace.measurement: Current totals + projected per-game rates x expected games (availability distribution) for each candidate; simulate race; check rule definitions (per-game vs total, minimum games).

nba.draft_board.label: Draft order, lottery odds and consensus prospect ranking
nba.draft_board.mechanism: Draft markets depend on lottery outcomes (odds table), team needs and consensus big boards/mock drafts.
nba.draft_board.rationale: Pick position and consensus ranking jointly drive who is selected; lottery odds are fixed by the standings and rules; mock draft consensus moves in the final days with workouts and team intel. Subtle: draft-night trades change order, and the market may lead the public mocks.
nba.draft_board.measurement: Lottery odds from standings and rules, consensus rank aggregated across public big boards/mocks, rank volatility near draft, trade-rumor flags.
free_sources: Public mock-draft aggregators (e.g. Tankathon, free web)

nba.transaction_flow.label: Transaction-flow signals (rumors, cap/apron constraints, trade rules)
nba.transaction_flow.mechanism: Trades, signings and waivers are constrained by cap rules, apron limits, roster spots and timelines; rumors from reliable reporters move probability.
nba.transaction_flow.rationale: Whether a player is traded or signed depends on contract status, salary-matching constraints, roster counts, deadline dates and team context; an event market's probability is the product of rule feasibility and reporting. Subtle: reporter reliability and wording (talks vs agreed) differ greatly, and rule details come from the CBA.
nba.transaction_flow.measurement: Compile cap sheet, apron and roster constraints, trade deadline dates, reported-talks timeline; base rates of rumored deals completing by reporter and wording.
free_sources: Spotrac / RealGM / Pro Sports Transactions (free tiers: contracts, cap, transactions)

nba.org_stability.label: Coach/front-office stability (record vs expectation, tenure, ownership)
nba.org_stability.mechanism: Coaching-change and franchise events depend on performance vs expectation, tenure, contract state and ownership behavior.
