nba.org_stability.rationale: Firing risk increases with a sharp underperformance relative to preseason expectation and a short losing streak, with timing driven by schedule breaks and ownership style. Subtle: these events are rare and noisy; base rates by team history matter more than record alone.
nba.org_stability.measurement: Wins vs preseason expectation, consecutive losses, coach tenure, contract/extension news, ownership turnover history; hazard model with sparse-event priors.
free_sources: Spotrac / RealGM / Pro Sports Transactions (free tiers: contracts, cap, transactions)

nba.all_star_process.label: All-Star voting/selection, captains and event participation
nba.all_star_process.mechanism: Fan/player/media voting and league announcements determine starters, reserves, contest entrants and event outcomes.
nba.all_star_process.rationale: All-Star outcomes are driven by published vote tallies (fan, player, media weights), selection rules and injuries/availability; event participation announcements are dated and sourced. Subtle: weights and eligibility rules change by year and the market often resolves on official announcement wording.
nba.all_star_process.measurement: Public vote leaderboards over time, weight formula, historical rank-to-selection conversion, injury status and eligibility; for contests, announced participants and past winners' profiles.

nba.calendar_announcements.label: Official calendar and announcement timing (schedule release, deadlines, dates)
nba.calendar_announcements.mechanism: Scheduled league announcements (schedule release, deadlines, draft dates) follow regular timing patterns that determine event-resolution markets.
nba.calendar_announcements.rationale: When the answer is a date or a content of an official announcement, past years' timing and leaks are the best prior. Subtle: unofficial leaks precede official release; wording of the resolution source controls settlement.
nba.calendar_announcements.measurement: Historical release dates by year, announced calendar, leak-to-release lags, content-pattern history (e.g. Christmas games).

nba.summer_league_minutes.label: Summer League rosters, minutes plans and rookie usage
nba.summer_league_minutes.mechanism: Summer League games feature unstable rosters, rookie/two-way minutes plans and shortened rotations, making roles and pace less predictable.
nba.summer_league_minutes.rationale: Teams use Summer League to evaluate young players, often with explicit minute caps or rotations, and lineup announcements arrive late. Subtle: little data per player, and team strength priors are weak; heavy uncertainty and different pace/total behavior than regular season.
nba.summer_league_minutes.measurement: Roster list with draft status/two-way contract, previous-year Summer League usage, announced minutes plans, game-day scratches; league-level pace and scoring baseline for Summer League.
free_sources: NBA Summer League box scores (nba.com, free)

nba.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rates for NBA off-court events
nba.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: Franchise, rule and personnel events occur at historical frequencies tied to the calendar.
nba.offfield_base_rate.rationale: These contracts cannot be modelled from game data; the honest prior is the frequency of the event class by calendar window, updated by dated reporting. Subtle: markets often over-price dramatic events relative to base rates.
nba.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Count events of the class per season and calendar window from news archives and league announcements; shrink with an empirical-Bayes prior; record the announcement timestamp.
free_sources: Wikipedia event timelines (as an index, verify against primary sources)

nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.label: Qualifying-games ledger (65 games with 20+ minutes) and slack
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.mechanism: The award eligibility count is a deterministic ledger that only the league's definition of a qualifying game updates; slack to the line plus injury hazard gives the probability of staying eligible.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.rationale: The existing eligibility input restates the rule but not the arithmetic; a player at 50 qualifying games with 20 left has a very different conditional risk from one at 62 with a nagging injury, and games of 15-20 minutes count only in a small allowance.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.measurement: Per player: qualifying = games with minutes >= 20 (allow up to 2 games of 15-20 minutes per league rule, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the 2026-27 rule); slack = games_remaining - (65 - qualifying); P(eligible) = P(missed games among remaining <= slack) under a Poisson-binomial with per-game miss probability = player-season availability rate shrunk with k=20 games toward position prior, updated nightly after the 6pm ET injury report; as-of timestamp = last completed game. Apply the ledger only to awards the league criteria say it governs (flag per award; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), and not to monthly awards, Coach or Executive of the Year, All-Star selection or draft markets.

nba.award_role_filters.label: Award-specific candidate filters (bench-start ratio, rookie status, clutch minimum)
nba.award_role_filters.mechanism: Each award has a definitional filter (Sixth Man must come off the bench in more games than he starts, ROY needs rookie status, Clutch POY needs clutch minutes/games, MIP needs improvement versus prior year) that decides who is in the candidate set.
nba.award_role_filters.rationale: A single input called award_stats treats all awards alike, but the candidate set is built by the filter first; a starter promoted mid-season loses Sixth Man eligibility, and a rookie who played overseas may or may not be a rookie.
nba.award_role_filters.measurement: Per award: boolean membership computed from the league definition on as-of date: sixth man requires games_off_bench > games_started; ROY requires rookie flag from the league rookie list; Clutch POY requires clutch minutes (last 5 min, score within 5) >= league minimum; produce candidate list and the gap in the stat the award names (clutch net points, improvement delta in PER/BPM, defensive win shares) with 10-game shrinkage to season value.

nba.expectation_overperformance.label: Wins minus preseason expectation (own, non-market)
nba.expectation_overperformance.mechanism: Coach, Executive, MIP and team-driven awards reward results above what the roster implied before the season, so voters compare wins to a preseason baseline.
nba.expectation_overperformance.rationale: Total wins alone ranks the best teams first, but Coach of the Year goes to the largest positive surprise; the baseline must be an own rating-based preseason projection and not a sportsbook win total to avoid a market-derived input.
nba.expectation_overperformance.measurement: exp_wins_pre = 82 x (own preseason team rating converted via Pythagorean with exponent 14, using returning minutes-weighted player ratings with 0.6 weight on last season, 0.4 on career, regressed 30% to league mean); surprise = wins_to_date - exp_wins_pre scaled by sd 6 wins; recompute on the as-of date using games played to date + 82 - GP times current rating.

nba.allnba_points_ladder.label: All-NBA points ladder and cut-line margins (positionless)
nba.allnba_points_ladder.mechanism: All-NBA teams are three five-player cut lines on a single points ranking (5/3/1 for first/second/third team); a candidate's probabilities across team markets are nested.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.rationale: Candidates with similar profiles split votes and a margin of a few points moves a player between teams; ballots are positionless since 2023-24, so the old guard/forward/center constraints no longer bind and should not be modelled.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.measurement: Simulate 100 ballots: each voter draws a ranked 15-player list from a Dirichlet-perturbed consensus of candidates' production and team-success scores (concentration alpha=8 per candidate, calibrated to 2023-25 published vote totals); output P(rank<=5), P(rank<=10), P(rank<=15), enforce sums of 5, 10, 15; as-of nightly after the eligibility filter.
free_sources: Official All-NBA voting totals (published after announcement)

nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.label: Draft pick ownership graph with protections and swaps
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.mechanism: Which franchise holds slot N depends on lottery results filtered through traded-pick protections, swap rights and conveyance order across years.
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.rationale: Team-to-draft and slot markets require knowing owner(s) and conditions; an unconditional top-4 protected pick converts to a future obligation and changes incentives of both teams in the standings race.
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.measurement: Table per pick: original team, current owner, protection (top-N range), swap counterpart and conveyance date; for each lottery outcome, determine slot and holder using the protection rules; as-of timestamp = latest completed trade; join with simulated standings to yield P(owner holds slot k).

nba.prospect_board_dispersion.label: Prospect consensus rank and cross-board dispersion
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.mechanism: Selection at slot N is a categorical outcome over the top prospects; disagreement across public boards and team-specific mocks signals entropy and information arrival.
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.rationale: A single consensus rank hides that the second pick is nearly deterministic in some drafts and a coin flip among four prospects in others; measuring dispersion is the correct uncertainty input.
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.measurement: For each prospect: mean and sd of rank across at least 6 boards (ESPN, The Athletic, Tankathon, NBADraft.net, Bleacher Report, Yahoo) with weights proportional to each source's historical rank-error; convert to P(selected at slot k) by a Plackett-Luce model fit on 2015-2025 drafts; update after each workout/medical report with 48h half-life.

nba.monthly_window_schedule.label: Games-in-window and schedule for monthly awards
nba.monthly_window_schedule.mechanism: Monthly player/rookie/coach/defender awards depend on games played inside the window, with fewer games for a candidate lowering his total counting stats and chance of an extreme month.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.rationale: Players on teams with 12 games in the window versus 16 have different expected volume; the conference split of winners and ties matters for pro-rata payout.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.measurement: games_in_window per candidate team from the league schedule; expected counting stats = per-game mean x games with 10-game shrinkage; probability of winning within conference = softmax over candidates of standardized (points, wins, efficiency) with temperature fit on past months; update on the as-of date.

nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.label: All-Star starter composite (fan 50% / player 25% / media 25%) and positional slot arithmetic
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.mechanism: Starters are the top weighted-average ranks within position groups per conference: each candidate's rank in the fan vote, the current-player vote and the media vote is combined 50/25/25 and the best composite fill two backcourt and three frontcourt slots in each conference.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.rationale: KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR are not decided by the ballot of about 100 media voters in stage s4: the fan vote carries half the weight, is public in early-return snapshots during the voting window, and depends on market size and social following, while the player and media votes follow production. The slot arithmetic (guard versus frontcourt, per conference) decides who is displaced.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.measurement: For each candidate and conference compute composite = 0.50 x fan_rank + 0.25 x player_rank + 0.25 x media_rank within the guard or frontcourt group; fan_rank at close = last published early-return rank plus a random-walk adjustment scaled by the share of voting window remaining (estimate step variance from past years' return snapshots), with the prior from last year's final fan rank, market size and social following; player and media ranks from the production rank in nba.award_stats with beta noise estimated from past ballot-vs-stat rank gaps; starters = lowest composites filling 2 guard and 3 frontcourt slots per conference (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the 2027 formula and slot split); simulate 10,000 draws and report P(starter) per candidate.
free_sources: Wayback Machine snapshots of fan-vote leaderboards

nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.label: All-Star reserve selection by coaches (7 per conference) and injury replacement
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.mechanism: After starters are fixed, conference head coaches vote for seven reserves each (not their own players) and the commissioner names injury replacements, so P(All-Star) for a non-starter is the chance of ranking among the best remaining players by position and wildcard slots.
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.rationale: KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR settle on the full roster, so reserve probability matters as much as starter probability; coaches value team record and recent play more than fan appeal, and an injured selectee is replaced by a commissioner choice that is hard to forecast.
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.measurement: For each non-starter candidate: coach-vote score = z-score of production rank (nba.award_stats) plus team win% rank, calibrated to past reserve selections by logistic regression on 10 seasons with position group and conference as strata; P(reserve) = P(rank among the 7 reserve slots after starters are removed) via 10,000 simulations conditional on the starter simulation; injury-replacement probability = P(a selectee is injured) x P(commissioner picks the next-ranked player); the 2 wildcard slots are position-free (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for 2027 rules).

nba.voter_signal_proxy.label: Observable voter-signal proxy: public media ladders, prior-win count and repeat-winner penalty
nba.voter_signal_proxy.mechanism: Replaces the unmeasurable narrative and voter-fatigue notion with observables: average rank in published media award ladders and straw polls, the number of consecutive prior wins, and the candidate's first-place share in the previous two seasons.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.rationale: nba.voting_narrative is audited WEAK because it is not measurable as defined, yet narrative and fatigue are the only drivers of the vote beyond production and team success; a proxy built from public ladders and past ballots gives them a measurable form without using any market price.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.measurement: For each candidate and award: mean rank over the last 4 published media ladders (NBA.com ladder, ESPN straw poll; unranked = 6th) with weights 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 newest first; repeat_penalty = number of consecutive prior wins; prior_share = first-place vote share in the last two seasons (0 if not a finalist); fit a conditional-logit ballot model on 2000-2026 winners with these three features plus production rank and seed, shrinking coefficients with a ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-season-out.

nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture weights and component rates
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: Minutes are a mixture of regimes (blowout truncation, normal, foul-limited, OT, restricted) whose weights depend on game state and each regime has different per-minute stat rates.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: The existing nba.minutes is a point projection that hides the multimodality; for a threshold sum, P(S>=25) is driven by the weight of the full-minutes regime, not by the mean minutes.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: From 3+ seasons of play-by-play, classify each player-game into regimes by the minutes and score margin (blowout: |margin|>=18 with 4th-quarter minutes<8; foul-limited: >=4 fouls by Q3; OT; restriction: coach-announced); fit regime weights as a multinomial logit of (own-model spread, rest, opponent pace, bench depth) with ridge shrinkage; each regime's stat-per-minute rates estimated with 15-game half-life and a prior from players of the same role; as-of timestamp = last injury report vintage.

nba.early_exit_hazard.label: Protected-void probability: first-half-only participation (injury, ejection, illness or coach-rested second half)
nba.early_exit_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters in the first half but never after halftime, including OT) = injury/ejection/illness exit hazard plus the coach decision to rest him for the whole second half in a lopsided game; the protected clause voids both unless the strike was already reached.
nba.early_exit_hazard.rationale: Early exit by injury is only one route to the void state: the sampled protected text voids any player who enters in the first half and does not enter after it, so a starter pulled for the entire second half of a first-half blowout is also void. Both routes are unrelated to per-minute rates and the second is strongly tied to the first-half margin.
nba.early_exit_hazard.measurement: Two components over the last 3 seasons. (a) Injury/ejection/illness exit hazard h = exits (left and did not return) / minutes, shrunk to a position prior with k=2000 minutes and scaled by 1.5 for the first 3 games after a listed injury; P(exit before half) = 1 - exp(-h*minutes_in_half1). (b) Coach-rest route: from play-by-play, P(no second-half entry | played first half and non-injury) by own-model pregame spread bucket and coach, estimated on 3 seasons with beta shrinkage k=30 games; combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b); then convert by contract wording (protected void vs actual stats, with the strike-already-reached carve-out).

nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.label: Lineup-conditional per-100 rates for points, rebounds and assists
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.mechanism: The three components move differently when teammates are on or off court: a creator off court raises the player's usage and assists, a big off court raises rebounds.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.rationale: Season-average per-minute rates blur lineup regimes, and teammate_absence_shift is a single directional signal; separate rates per partner set are needed for a sum that moves in offsetting directions.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.measurement: Per player: per-100-possession PTS, REB, AST computed by on-court partner set (with/without each of the top-3 teammates by minutes), minimum 300 possessions per cell, empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the player's overall rate with k=400 possessions; applied to tonight's expected lineup from the confirmed or projected starters; as-of = latest lineup information.

nba.own_game_environment.label: Own-model game environment (team points, possessions)
nba.own_game_environment.mechanism: Both teams' scoring environment determines how many scoring chances exist in the minutes played.
nba.own_game_environment.rationale: nba.implied_team_totals is derived from the sportsbook spread and total, which is market-derived, so it should be a benchmark; an own estimate from ratings and pace gives an independent environment.
nba.own_game_environment.measurement: Team points = pace_own x (opponent-adjusted ORtg) / 100 using 20-game exponentially weighted ratings with opponent adjustment by ridge (lambda tuned on 2 prior seasons); possessions = geometric mean of the two teams' opponent-adjusted pace; adjustment for tonight's active set via lineup rating deltas; output team points and sd.

nba.first_possession_chain_prob.label: Opening-possession race probability (team scores first)
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.mechanism: Probability that team A scores first given tip result and each team's opening-possession conversion rate: pA/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB)).
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.rationale: The existing tip input treats tip win as the driver, but the tip only fixes who starts the race; the conversion rates on both sides decide it and the formula shows why the tip's effect is only a few points. At pA = pB = 0.5 the race formula gives 0.667 for the team holding the ball, so a tip win is worth about 2-3 points of team-first probability, not more.
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.measurement: pA = team A opening-possession scoring proxy under the contract definition: share of games in which A's first trip produced a made FG (if free throws do not count) or at least one made shot or free throw (if they do), computed over last 2 seasons with 15-game half-life and shrunk to league 0.50 with k=40 games; pB similar for B; P(A first) = P(A wins tip) * pA/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB)) + (1-P(A wins tip)) * [1 - pB/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB))]; P(A wins tip) = 0.5 + 0.1*(jumper tip rate - 0.5) with the two starting jumpers' last-two-season tip win rates shrunk with k=15 tips.

nba.early_game_usage_first6.label: Early-game usage (first six minutes) by starter
nba.early_game_usage_first6.mechanism: The share of team shot attempts and made baskets taken by each starter in the first six minutes of the game, where scripted plays and starter minutes dominate.
nba.early_game_usage_first6.rationale: First-basket history is a handful of events per player; the first six minutes of play produce far more observations (about 12-18 attempts per team per game) and reflect the script.
nba.early_game_usage_first6.measurement: Per starter: FGA+0.44*FTA share and made-FG share within the first 6 minutes of Q1 across last 60 games (half-life 25), shrunk toward the player's overall usage with k=120 early-game team attempts; renormalise across tonight's expected starters; combine with first_basket_share by precision weighting.

nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.label: First-attempt shot-type mix and make probability
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.mechanism: The opening shot is more likely a rim attempt or a catch-and-shoot three off a set play, and the make rate depends on that type.
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.rationale: The existing shot_profile is season-wide but the opening plays use their own distribution; a player whose first shots are layups has a higher conversion than the same player's season average.
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.measurement: From the first FGA of each team-game for 3 seasons, tabulate type (rim, corner 3, above-break 3, mid) per player; make probability = type-specific league rate (rim .62, corner 3 .38, ATB 3 .36, mid .42, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) shrunk to the player's type-specific rate with k=50 attempts; weight by tonight's opponent allowed rate in that zone for the first 6 minutes.

nba.starting_five_continuity.label: Starting-five continuity (games together)
nba.starting_five_continuity.mechanism: The opening set depends on practiced combinations; a new starting five or a replaced starter resets the first-possession script.
nba.starting_five_continuity.rationale: First-basket shares computed with a different starter are stale; the number of games the current five has started together tells how much of the history to trust.
nba.starting_five_continuity.measurement: Count of consecutive and total games the exact tonight's starting five has started together this season and last, plus overlap measured as the number of the five who started the last 10 games; weight for historical first-shot shares = min(1, games_together/15) and the rest reverts to role-based priors (position, usage).

nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.label: Non-additive multi-absence cost curve
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.mechanism: The margin cost of losing several rotation players is not the sum of individual costs because the replacement pool deteriorates and rotations compress.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.rationale: The existing catalog sums per-player impact (player_impact, lineup_adj_rating) but missing two starters on a team with a deep bench costs less than two times one, whereas on a thin team it costs more; the curve must be estimated by roster depth.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.measurement: Fit on 5 seasons of team-games: margin residual vs number of missing rotation players (top-8 by minutes) and the sum of their impact values, with spline in missing impact and interaction with depth index (average impact of players 9-12); predictions per scenario branch; shrink spline with ridge; as-of nightly after injury report.

nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.label: Replacement-level minutes absorption
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.mechanism: When a rotation player is out, minutes flow to specific teammates at specific quality; who absorbs them (a starter playing more versus a bench player starting) determines the actual rating loss.
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.rationale: Impact-based absence valuations assume replacement at team-average bench quality; a team whose next man up is a two-way player or an out-of-position player loses much more.
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.measurement: From 3 seasons of game-level minutes: for each team and absent role (primary ball handler, wing, rim protector), estimate the share of vacated minutes absorbed by each teammate with ridge regression, then compute expected replaced rating = Σ share_j × impact_j(minutes-adjusted); use 20-game half-life; compare to team default; fallback to position-group priors for new combinations.

nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.label: Roster-overlap weighted team rating
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.mechanism: Past game results are weighted by how similar the active set of that game was to tonight's, so results from games with different rosters count less.
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.rationale: Season ratings blend games played with and without stars, and a rating from a healthy-roster sample misleads for a depleted lineup; the overlap weighting makes the baseline condition on the rotation.
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.measurement: Weight w_g = exp(-lambda × (1 - overlap_g)) × recency half-life 40 games, overlap_g = Σ over tonight's top-10 players of min_share_tonight × I(played in game g), lambda fit by out-of-sample game-margin error on 3 seasons; rating = weighted opponent-adjusted net rating shrunk to the preseason prior with k=15 effective games.

nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.label: Pace- and total-dependent margin standard deviation (own-model, not line-based)
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.mechanism: Margin variance scales with possession count and total scoring, and with spread through garbage time.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.rationale: The existing score_resid is defined around lines, which is market-derived; the variance should come from the game's own pace/total estimates so that cover probabilities at wide spreads are correct.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.measurement: Fit sd_margin = a + b × sqrt(own-model possessions) + c × |own-model mean margin| on 5 seasons of team-games (own predictions, not closing lines); report quantile curves (10/25/50/75/90) with a skew parameter for heavy favourites; validate by the probability integral transform per bucket.

nba.series_game_conditional_state.label: Playoff-series game-conditional state
nba.series_game_conditional_state.mechanism: In a series, a game's mean margin depends on series score, rest days between games, accumulated injuries and coaching adjustments.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.rationale: Single-game ratings treat games as independent; series markets (home clinch, game 7, comeback) depend on the dependency between games and on elimination-state minutes tightening.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.measurement: Features: games played, series score, rest days since the last game, minutes of the stars in the previous game, margin of the previous game, injury-status change since game 1; fit a hierarchical model of game margin residual on 2000-2025 series with series-level random effect (sd about 2 points) and elimination-game dummy; as-of the last completed game.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from nba.margin sd model (about 12, scale sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.

nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.label: Coach-level tie-forcing and intentional-foul policy
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.mechanism: How often a team trailing by 2-3 in the last 30 seconds attempts a tying three or a fast two, and how often the leading team fouls up three.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.rationale: Excess tie mass comes from end-of-game choices; teams differ, and the same game state yields a tie more often when the trailing coach shoots for the tie than when he fouls and hopes.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: in games within 3 points with <30 seconds left, share of trailing-team possessions ending in a 3PA, a 2PA or a foul-drawn FT; leading-team foul-up-3 rate; compute per coach over 3 seasons (min 15 events) with shrinkage k=10 events to league mean; produce per-matchup tie-conditional probability = P(close at 30s) × P(tie | close, policies).

nba.ot_period_distribution.label: Distribution of number of overtime periods and OT scoring
nba.ot_period_distribution.mechanism: If overtime occurs, additional periods occur with a small probability and each period adds a fixed block of minutes and points.
nba.ot_period_distribution.rationale: The count of OT periods matters for series OT markets and for strike markets on total, bench or team stats within the family; the draft treats OT as one event.
nba.ot_period_distribution.measurement: Empirical P(k OT periods) from 15 seasons: P(1), P(2), P(3+) conditional on OT; per-period points per team sampled from the league distribution adjusted for pace (mean about 11-12 per team per 5 minutes, sd 5); update yearly; for series OT: P(at least one OT game) = sum over series length L of P(L) * (1 - prod over games g of (1 - p_g)), with P(L) from nba.series_model (4-7 games, shorter for mismatched teams) and p_g from nba.reg_tie_pmf_model using each game's own-model margin; inflate the variance across games because closeness is positively correlated within a series (estimate by the observed share of series with >=1 OT game versus the independent prediction on 15 seasons of playoff series). The settled quantity (at least one OT game, or a count) is unsampled, see u6.

nba.bench_minutes_distribution.label: Bench minutes distribution (240 + 25k minus starter minutes)
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.mechanism: Bench points depend on bench minutes first; they equal total team minutes minus starter minutes and shrink when starters play heavy minutes in close games or OT.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.rationale: The draft's bench input is points share, while the better predictor is minutes times points per minute with a state-dependent minutes distribution.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.measurement: Per team: bench minutes = 240 + 25*OT - Σ starter minutes; model starter minutes as scenario mixture (blowout/close/OT/foul trouble) with weights from own-model margin; bench points = bench minutes × bench points-per-minute with 30-game half-life and shrinkage k=300 minutes; as-of lineups; output mean/sd by scenario.
free_sources: nba_api box score minutes and starters

nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.label: Starter/bench designation ledger and rest-driven reclassification
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.mechanism: The bench is the set of players not in the official starting five, so a starter absence promotes the next man into the starter group and shifts scoring from bench to starter.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.rationale: The draft interaction says a rested starter becomes a bench player, but a rested starter does not play; the real effects are (a) a promoted bench player moves out of the bench count and (b) a returning star on a restriction coming off the bench moves in.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.measurement: Record for each team-game: official starters list, status of expected starters, bench designation of the primary scorers; compute counterfactual bench points under tonight's starter list using player points-per-minute and projected minutes: bench_pts = Σ_{non-starters} proj_min × ppm; adjust for returning player minute limits; as-of lineup confirmation.

nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.label: Team-stat pair difference model (shared-pace correlation)
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.mechanism: The head-to-head team stat is the difference of two counts with positive correlation through game pace and negative through script effects.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.rationale: Treating the two teams' counts as independent overstates the sd of the difference and misprices the zero-tie mass.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.measurement: For team stat X (e.g. 3PM): mean_X = attempts_X × rate_X using opponent-adjusted rates (20-game half-life, k=150 attempts); sd_diff from joint empirical covariance over 3 seasons: var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B with rho from pace; compute P(A>B), P(tie) with discrete negative binomial convolution; blowout correction increasing trailing-team attempts.

nba.game_pace_composition.label: Game-pace composition rule from two teams' tempos
nba.game_pace_composition.mechanism: Expected game possessions as a function of both teams' pace, transition frequency and turnover rates rather than a simple average.
nba.game_pace_composition.rationale: The draft states that the slower team controls tempo; the empirical rule must be fitted, with transition frequency and defence-forced turnovers as additional terms.
nba.game_pace_composition.measurement: Regress game possessions on (paceA + paceB)/2, |paceA - paceB|, each team's transition-frequency and turnover rate and rest, using 5 seasons of team-games with opponent-adjusted paces (20-game half-life); report coefficients and residual sd; as-of the last completed game; adjust for active set via nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decomposition.

nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.label: Absence effect split into pace and efficiency components
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.mechanism: Each rotation player's absence changes team pace and ORtg/DRtg separately, with different signs by role.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.rationale: The existing lineup_adj_rating collapses availability into one net rating, which is the right variable for margin but wrong for totals where a slower-and-worse offence and a faster-and-weaker defence have opposite effects.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.measurement: For each player with at least 800 minutes: on/off differences in team possessions per 48, ORtg and DRtg over 3 seasons with ridge shrinkage (k=600 possessions) and teammate adjustment (RAPM-style regression on pace as well); apply to tonight's scenario weights; as-of nightly after injury report.

nba.three_point_variance_load.label: Three-point attempt volume as a variance load
nba.three_point_variance_load.mechanism: The sd of the total depends on how many threes both teams attempt and on the dispersion of free-throw and two-point results.
nba.three_point_variance_load.rationale: The draft says total sd is about 17-19 as a constant; it varies with shot mix, and wide-open three-heavy teams produce a wider total distribution that matters at ladder tails.
nba.three_point_variance_load.measurement: Var_total = Σ_team [9*3PA*p3(1-p3) + 4*2PA*p2(1-p2) + FTA*pft(1-pft)] + var(possessions)*ppp^2*... using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life); calibrate a scale factor lambda so that predicted variance matches realised total residual variance in 2 prior seasons; report sd per game and skew.

nba.series_length_distribution.label: Series-length distribution from per-game win probabilities
nba.series_length_distribution.mechanism: The number of games in a best-of-seven series is a function of per-game win probability, home pattern and dependence between games.
nba.series_length_distribution.rationale: KXNBASERIESGAMES counts games, not points; the draft has no input for it except a generic series model reference outside the archetype.
nba.series_length_distribution.measurement: P(series ends in k games) by dynamic programming over home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 with per-game win probabilities from own-model ratings and series dependence parameter (game-to-game correlation about +0.05 on margin, estimated from 2000-2025 playoff series); injuries known as of the as-of date; output P(4), P(5), P(6), P(7).

nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.label: Empirical final-margin pmf by own-model mean and sd
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.mechanism: The final margin has non-smooth pmf structure (hole at zero, OT bump, late-game parity) that a normal density does not reproduce.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.rationale: The draft names score_resid as the margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets from market lines are circular and the pmf structure lives at the integer level; band edges at 5/6 and 10/11 fall exactly on such structure.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.measurement: Collect 15 seasons of final signed margins; standardise z = (margin - mu_own)/sigma_own using own-model mean and sd; estimate the pmf of the integer margin by kernel smoothing of the z-density plus an explicit multiplicative correction per integer margin in [-12, 12] (ridge-shrunk to 1); validate by log-loss of band probabilities in 2 held-out seasons; recompute annually.

nba.margin_decay_after_pull.label: Margin decay after starters are pulled (by coach and lead size)
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.mechanism: The final margin equals the margin at the pull time plus a bench-vs-bench drift whose size depends on lead and coach.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.rationale: Blowout probability alone does not tell how much a 20-point lead at 6:00 shrinks; a coach who pulls starters early gives up points.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.measurement: From play-by-play: margin at the time both starters of the leading team are out and the final margin; compute mean and sd of the change by lead bucket (10-14, 15-19, 20+) and by coach with 3 seasons of data, shrunk to league with k=8 games; as-of the last completed game; output drift and sd for tonight's coaches.

nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.label: Second-unit net rating gap
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.mechanism: The bench lineups play most late blowout minutes, so the margin drift is the second unit's net rating difference.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.rationale: Starter-based team ratings say nothing about who wins the last six minutes of a blowout; a deep bench preserves a lead.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.measurement: Net rating of the lineups with at most one top-5 player, per 100 possessions, over the last 40 games with opponent adjustment and shrinkage k=250 possessions; gap = team A second unit minus team B second unit; translate to expected margin drift per 6 minutes = gap × 12/100; as-of rotation as projected.

nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.label: Final-margin pmf conditional on overtime
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.mechanism: If regulation ties, the final margin is the margin of a five-minute period (or more), concentrated in 1-8 points.
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.rationale: Mass of the lowest bands is the sum of a regulation part and an OT part; the OT part follows a different distribution with folded structure.
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.measurement: Empirical pmf of |final margin| for games with OT_periods = 1, 2, 3+ over 15 seasons; fit folded-normal with sd s_OT estimated by maximum likelihood (about 6-7 for one OT); combine with P(OT) from the tie model: P(band) = P(reg in band)(1-P(OT)) + P(OT) × P(OT margin in band).

nba.governance_approval_pipeline.label: Deal-stage ledger and league approval pipeline
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.mechanism: Sales, relocations and expansions pass through stages (exploration, exclusivity, definitive agreement, governance vote, closing) with stage-specific completion odds and delays.
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.rationale: A rumor-level input cannot tell whether a deal is two weeks or five months from the qualifying stage, and the contracts require specific stages; the pipeline gives P(complete by date).
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.measurement: For each live deal record stage, date entered, and the historical distribution of days to the next stage from past NBA and other major-league sales (log-normal fit per stage, shrunk to cross-league pooled values with k=3 deals); compute P(reach required stage by T) = Π P(transition) × P(duration sum <= T-t); update when a stage is entered; attach the league approval vote threshold as a feasibility gate (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the exact threshold).

nba.reporter_reliability_score.label: Reporter and source reliability by report stage
nba.reporter_reliability_score.mechanism: Conversion probability of a report into the qualifying event depends on the reporter and the claim stage (talks, agreed in principle, finalising).
nba.reporter_reliability_score.rationale: The draft input 'transactions, trades, coaching news' is a feed, not a probability; the value is a calibration table P(event | source, stage).
nba.reporter_reliability_score.measurement: Compile reports from tier-one national reporters and team beat writers over 5 seasons, label each with stage (talks / agreed / done), compute completion rate and median lead time to the official act per source and stage with beta-binomial shrinkage k=10 reports; apply to tonight's reports with time decay half-life 7 days for 'talks'; as-of report timestamp.

nba.calendar_hazard_profile.label: Calendar hazard profile (deadlines, draft, free agency, board meetings)
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.mechanism: Event hazard varies with landmarks: trade deadline, draft week, free-agency opening, league board meetings, season start.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.rationale: A uniform hazard over the window badly misprices markets with a deadline; most transactions cluster in a few days and the remaining hazard collapses after each landmark.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.measurement: Estimate discrete-time hazard by day-of-year landmark offset from 15 seasons of transactions (trades, coach changes, retirements, signings) with kernel smoothing and a landmark dummy set; P(event in remaining window) = 1 - Π(1-h_d) with hazards conditioned on the event not having occurred; incorporate announced meeting dates as known spikes.

nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.label: Qualifying-stage requirement per contract wording
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.mechanism: Each series names which stage counts; a map from wording to stage lets the model score the right stage.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.rationale: The draft treats the wording as a text input, but the useful object is a coded stage per series and the exclusions list, so the same news can be mapped to Yes/No consistently.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.measurement: For each series code: required stage (announce / signed definitive / approved / adopted), time zone, window end, carve-outs and multi-outcome rules; fill from rules_primary and rules_secondary of every live series (22 here), mark TITLE_ONLY where no text; test with 20 historical events whether the wording would have resolved Yes.

nba.career_horizon_signals.label: Player career-horizon signals (age, contract years, injury, public statements)
nba.career_horizon_signals.mechanism: Retirement and next-contract markets depend on age, contract expiry, injury burden, role decline and public statements.
nba.career_horizon_signals.rationale: The draft input injury_risk_season is a season games-missed expectation, not a career-horizon hazard; retirement hazard rises with age and with specific signals such as a farewell tour announcement.
nba.career_horizon_signals.measurement: Per player: age, years remaining on contract, cumulative games missed over last two seasons, minutes trend, explicit retirement statements (coded 0/1/2 by explicitness), compute discrete hazard by age from historical retirements (e.g. age 38+ about 20-25% per year, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and multiply by an odds factor for explicit statements; effective date constraint from rule wording.

nba.player_move_destination_model.label: Player destination choice model with cap feasibility
nba.player_move_destination_model.mechanism: Destination is a choice among feasible teams determined by cap space or matching assets, team need, and player preference.
nba.player_move_destination_model.rationale: A multi-outcome next-team market needs a distribution over teams; relying on rumor misses cap constraints that exclude most teams.
nba.player_move_destination_model.measurement: For each candidate team compute feasibility (cap space or matching salaries within apron rules), asset fit and need (position gap, win-now vs rebuild); estimate a multinomial logit on 10 seasons of moves with these features plus player-preference flags (stated preference, agent reports); add a catch-all with probability from age and contract status; as-of nightly.

nba.rule_change_pipeline.label: Rule-change adoption pipeline (competition committee, Board of Governors vote calendar, trial history)
nba.rule_change_pipeline.mechanism: A rule change is adopted only after a proposal clears the competition committee and a Board of Governors vote at a scheduled meeting before the market window ends, so probability is the product of stage-transition rates and a calendar test.
nba.rule_change_pipeline.rationale: KXNBARULE (the "one free throw" rule adopted before the 2026-27 regular season) needs the committee and Board-of-Governors process, the meeting calendar and the history of proposals that were discussed but never adopted; the pooled off-field base rate says nothing about it.
nba.rule_change_pipeline.measurement: Build the list of publicly reported rule proposals 2000-2026 with stage reached (reported idea, committee discussion, committee recommendation, Board vote, adopted) and months from stage to adoption; P(adopt before date) = P(next stage cleared) x ... along the remaining stages x indicator that a scheduled Board meeting falls before the deadline; shrink stage rates toward the all-proposal rate with k=10 proposals; approval threshold (recalled as a three-quarters majority) SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
free_sources: NBA Board of Governors meeting releases

nba.franchise_valuation_comps.label: Franchise valuation reference class (comparable sale and expansion prices)
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.mechanism: A headline franchise value is drawn from the distribution of recent sale and expansion prices, scaled by market size and revenue growth, so P(value above strike) comes from a predictive distribution over comparables, not a base rate of events.
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.rationale: KXNBAFRANCHISECOST resolves on a headline enterprise value above a strike after bundled assets are stripped; the event base rate says only whether a sale happens, whereas the strike probability needs a valuation model built from comparable transactions and the league's expansion-fee reporting.
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.measurement: Collect headline enterprise values of NBA franchise sales and expansion fees 2015-2026 with market, year and reported separable asset adjustments; regress log(value) on the prior-year published franchise valuation, revenue growth and market size; predictive sd from residuals (inflate for expansion franchises, which have no comparables); P(headline > strike) from the predictive distribution, then multiply by P(qualifying sale announced and approved within the window) from the approval pipeline.

nba.game_factor_loadings.label: Game-level latent factor loadings by leg type
nba.game_factor_loadings.mechanism: Legs load on shared factors (pace/total, margin, team shooting luck, availability) with loadings that differ by leg type and player role.
nba.game_factor_loadings.rationale: The draft lists covariance of a single player's stats, but multi-leg dependence spans legs from different mechanisms; a factor model captures it with a manageable parameter count.
nba.game_factor_loadings.measurement: Fit a Gaussian-copula factor model on 6 seasons of game-level outcomes: observed leg indicators (spread covers, total overs, player N+ at typical thresholds) transformed to normal scores via marginal CDFs; estimate loadings with 3 factors (total, margin, team luck) per team-side and role cell (starter guard, wing, big) with ridge shrinkage; report loadings and sd across 100 bootstrap draws; as-of end of the previous game.

nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.label: Within-team scoring allocation dependence
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.mechanism: Teammates split a fixed team total, giving negative dependence between teammates' counts conditional on team points.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.rationale: Treating two teammates' overs as positively dependent through the team total omits the allocation effect that offsets it at fixed pace; the net sign depends on how much variation in the team total versus in the split drives each leg.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.measurement: For each team and pair of top-6 players, compute the correlation of player points conditional on team points (partial correlation) using 3 seasons of games, shrunk to the role-pair prior with k=40 games; combine with team total correlation to get unconditional pairwise correlations; separate regimes with/without a major teammate absence.

nba.leg_void_state.label: Leg void-state probabilities and combo payoff rule
nba.leg_void_state.mechanism: The combination's payoff depends on how a void leg (inactive player, protected early exit, postponement) is treated.
nba.leg_void_state.rationale: If one leg can void, the effective probability of Yes given not void differs from the product of the remaining legs, and the void probability itself is correlated with other legs through the injury event.
nba.leg_void_state.measurement: For each leg: P(void) = P(inactive) + P(protected early exit) + P(postponement beyond 48 hours) from the availability model; compute joint outcome probabilities for each void combination; apply the contract's rule (void whole, drop leg, or No) to compute the payoff probability; the rule is an input to be read from rules_primary when a combo series is live.

nba.own_model_team_totals.label: Own-model expected team points and total (market-free shared scoring factor)
nba.own_model_team_totals.mechanism: Expected team points = expected game possessions times availability-adjusted points per possession against the specific opponent, with a residual distribution built from own predictions; gives the shared scoring factor that same-game legs load on.
nba.own_model_team_totals.rationale: The shared pace/total factor must come from an own-model team total because a total implied by sportsbook lines is a market output and cannot serve as an input; this input also supplies the margin-total residual correlation that sportsbook-implied totals cannot.
nba.own_model_team_totals.measurement: possessions = pace composition of the two teams (nba.pace, lineup-aware, last 20 games weighted with half-life 8 games, shrunk to league mean with k=15 games); points per possession = availability-adjusted offence versus opponent defence rating with home adjustment, shrunk with k=20 games; team points = possessions x ppp; residual sd by team from own predictions on 5 seasons (not closing lines); output joint (margin, total) mean and covariance for the simulation.

nba.on_court_assist_share.label: On-court assist share of team assisted field goals
nba.on_court_assist_share.mechanism: The fraction of the team's assisted makes credited to the player while he is on the floor, which is the stable per-opportunity rate.
nba.on_court_assist_share.rationale: Potential assists and usage are indirect; the on-court assist share is the direct outcome rate, decomposed by lineup and whether co-creators are present, and is the cleanest basis for projecting the count from team assisted makes.
nba.on_court_assist_share.measurement: Share = player AST / (team assisted FGM while player on court), computed over last 60 games with half-life 25 games, separately for lineups with and without the top co-creator; shrink to role prior with k=300 on-court team assisted FGM; projected AST = share × expected team assisted FGM in projected minutes; as-of last game.

nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.label: Expected team assisted field goals in the player's minutes
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.mechanism: Team assisted makes depend on possessions, field-goal percentage, shot mix and the style-driven assisted rate.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.rationale: The draft uses implied team totals (market-derived) as the environment; an own estimate of assisted makes depends on assisted-rate by team and by opponent coverage, which totals do not capture.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.measurement: E[assisted FGM] = possessions(own pace composition) × FGA per possession × FG% (opponent-adjusted, 20-game half-life, k=150 FGA) × assisted rate (team assisted/FGM, opponent scheme adjustment, 20-game half-life, k=100 FGM); scale to player's projected minutes share; report mean and sd by game.

nba.co_creator_load.label: Co-creator load (ball-dominant teammates on court)
nba.co_creator_load.mechanism: The presence of another ball-dominant creator divides initiations and assists.
nba.co_creator_load.rationale: Usage alone cannot distinguish a lone primary creator from a two-creator backcourt; assists fall when the second creator is on the floor and rise when he is out.
nba.co_creator_load.measurement: For the player and each teammate compute time of possession and touches per minute over 60 games; co-creator load = sum of the other four players' expected time of possession per minute (from lineup minutes) minus the league-average of the role; regress player's potential assists per minute on load (ridge) with team fixed effects; compute with tonight's expected lineups and scenarios.
free_sources: NBA.com tracking time of possession (via nba_api)

nba.return_timeline_hazard.label: Return-from-injury timeline hazard by injury type
nba.return_timeline_hazard.mechanism: The probability a player has returned by a date follows a recovery time-to-event distribution with setbacks, not a point estimate.
nba.return_timeline_hazard.rationale: Reported timelines are lower bounds with setbacks; a return-by-date market is a CDF at a date, and the shape depends on the injury (ankle sprain versus stress fracture versus surgery).
nba.return_timeline_hazard.measurement: Weibull survival fit by injury category on 10 seasons of injuries (from the first reported timeline to the first appearance), parameters shrunk to the pooled category with k=8 cases; adjust for team disclosure style via the ratio of actual to reported timeline; P(return by T) = 1 - exp(-(t/scale)^shape) with t measured from the injury date; update at each report; as-of timestamp.

nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.label: Rare-make accrual rate (attempts per game x make probability x exposure)
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.mechanism: P(at least one make over the season) = 1 - exp(-sum over games of attempts x probability), a Poisson accrual with parameter uncertainty.
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.rationale: Non-shooters have an attempt rate that can change after an off-season shooting project; preseason attempts are the leading indicator, and the exposure window excludes playoffs and the Cup final.
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.measurement: lambda_g = 3PA per 36 (last 2 seasons with weight 0.4/0.6, preseason attempts added at weight 2.0 per game) x projected minutes/36 x p3 (player's last two seasons shrunk to the position prior 0.30 with k=40 attempts); exposure = expected regular-season games with minutes = P(available) per scheduled game over the 82-game schedule plus the expected number of Cup knockout games the team plays before the final (the sampled rule counts Cup games before the Championship game, so group and knockout games add exposure only to teams that advance; the final is excluded); P = 1 - E[exp(-lambda_total)] under Gamma(k,theta) for lambda with k=3; update after every game with new attempts.

nba.opening_night_starter_signals.label: Opening-night starter signals (camp lineups, preseason starts, coach statements)
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.mechanism: The first regular-season game's starting five is predicted from the preseason starting lineups, camp reports and coach statements, with strong incumbency.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.rationale: A season-opener market has no in-season history, so the signal is the preseason; the team's preseason starters in the final two preseason games are usually the opener's starters, but not always.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.measurement: Score for each player = 0.5 x indicator of starting both of the last 2 preseason games + 0.3 x last season's start share + 0.2 x coach statement (coded 0/0.5/1); map to probability via logistic fit on 8 seasons of opener starters; set to 0 if the status is out or doubtful; combine with injury probability; as-of 24 hours before the opener and again at confirmation.
free_sources: Preseason box scores (nba_api season type Pre Season)

nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.label: Two-player co-appearance probability with rest correlation
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.mechanism: The probability that both players appear in at least one same game (or in many) is a joint availability probability with positive dependence from team rest decisions.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.rationale: Treating two players' availability as independent overstates co-appearance when rest decisions are shared and understates it when injuries are independent.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.measurement: Per game, P(both play) = pA pB + rho sqrt(pA(1-pA)pB(1-pB)) with rho estimated from 5 seasons of pair data (team rest days, load management) shrunk to a role prior; over N games P(at least one overlap) = 1 - Π(1 - P_g) with a correction for injury duration (autocorrelation across games); update after each game.

nba.payout_schedule_operator.label: Payout schedule operator g(K) parsed from rules text
nba.payout_schedule_operator.mechanism: The contract's value is E[g(K)] where g is the payout table in the rules text, so the schedule is part of the model.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.rationale: The cubic schedule means value is dominated by the upper tail: for threes with mean 3 the payout at the mean is $0.027, but the expected payout is much higher because 5+ made threes pay $0.125 or more. The operator must therefore be part of the model, not a post-hoc transform.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.measurement: Implement the two live schedules exactly: points g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/50)^3)/10000 with y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s/2))); threes g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/10)^3)/10000 with y = min(10, s); parse any new schedule from rules_primary/rules_secondary into (band_lo, band_hi, payout) arrays and cap/void fields and check monotonicity against the formula; value = sum over k of P(K=k) g(k); compute sensitivity of value to mean, variance and P(K >= cap) by finite differences; version the parser by rules hash and flag unparsed tables.

nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.label: Probability of heavy-minutes games (38+ minutes, OT)
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.mechanism: The extreme counts come from nights with heavy minutes, whose probability depends on game closeness, depth and the coach's usage of the star.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.rationale: A single projected minutes figure hides the 10-20% of nights with 38+ minutes that produce the top bands, and nights with 20-25 minutes that produce the bottom ones.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.measurement: Per player: share of games with minutes >= 38 over the last 80 games (half-life 30), shrunk to role prior with k=15 games; condition on own-model closeness (P(|margin| < 8) from the margin model) and OT probability 0.06; produce P(minutes >= 38) and mean count in that regime = rate per minute x 40; as-of lineup status.

nba.within_game_make_dispersion.label: Within-game make-rate dispersion (beta-binomial rho)
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.mechanism: Makes in a game are positively correlated beyond independent shots, so the count is overdispersed relative to a binomial.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.rationale: Independence understates the tail of makes, which a convex payout over-weights; the dispersion parameter is a key tail parameter.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.measurement: Estimate rho by maximum likelihood of a beta-binomial model on 5 seasons of player-game (attempts, makes) for players with at least 200 attempts; pool by shot type (three, two, free throw) and by attempt count; shrink the player-specific rho to the pooled value with k=100 games; produce the pmf of makes given attempts n and rate p.

nba.points_parity_band_mass.label: Composite points pmf with parity and free-throw effect for 2-point bands
nba.points_parity_band_mass.mechanism: Points = 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FT; the mass of a 2-point band depends on parity coming from threes and free throws.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.rationale: Band probabilities from a smooth normal approximation ignore the lattice structure of the composite, which can misallocate up to several percentage points between adjacent bands.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.measurement: Simulate FG2, FG3, FT counts with beta-binomial dispersion and component correlations estimated on 5 seasons; tabulate P(points = k) and aggregate to band edges from the rules; verify pmf mod 2 against historical frequencies; shrink the pmf to the smoothed empirical pmf of similar-usage players with weight 0.2.

nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.label: Field-goal attempts per minute split into two-point and three-point attempts, with free-throw trip rate
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.mechanism: Points = 2 x made 2PT + 3 x made 3PT + FTM, so each component needs its own attempt rate per minute rather than a blended usage rate that includes turnovers.
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.rationale: The points escalator needs FGA per minute by type and free-throw trips per minute as the volume base for the cubic payout; usage rate mixes in turnovers and free-throw trips, and the audit of nba.usage asks for this replacement.
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.measurement: 2PA, 3PA and FTA per 36 minutes over the last 2 seasons with weights 0.6 recent / 0.4 prior and half-life 20 games, shrunk to the role-position mean with k=300 minutes; scale by the projected minutes scenario mixture and add the with/without-teammate shift from the teammate-absence splits; output a per-minute rate and its sd for use in a negative-binomial attempt model.

nba.ft_trip_structure_model.label: Free-throw trip generation model (trips x attempts per trip)
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.mechanism: Attempts are the sum of trips (shooting fouls, bonus fouls, technicals, intentional fouls) times attempts per trip (1, 2, 3).
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.rationale: The draft's ft_attempts is a rate; the clustered structure of trips matters for the variance and for the survival function at N.
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.measurement: Per player: trips per 36 = shooting-foul trips (per 100 rim attempts and per 100 post touches) + bonus trips (per team-bonus minute) + other; attempts per trip distribution from his shot mix (share of 3PA fouled, and-one rate); estimate with 3 seasons of play-by-play, shrinkage k=60 trips to position prior; simulate trips with negative-binomial dispersion estimated across games.

nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.label: Bonus-state and team-foul environment
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.mechanism: Non-shooting fouls turn into free throws once the defending team is in the bonus, so the opponent's team foul rate and bonus minutes drive attempts.
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.rationale: Opponent foul rate enters twice (shooting fouls and bonus fouls), and the draft's foul rate input does not separate the bonus effect.
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.measurement: Opponent team personal fouls per quarter, share of quarter minutes in bonus (from play-by-play), crew fouls per game; combine as bonus_minutes_expected = f(opponent foul rate, crew rate, own pace) using 3 seasons; each bonus minute adds a rate of player-specific non-shooting-foul attempts (estimated from the player's FTA in bonus vs non-bonus minutes with shrinkage k=40 minutes).

nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.label: Intentional-foul target probability (hack-a policy and late-game ball handlers)
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.mechanism: Probability that the player is fouled intentionally in the last two minutes of a close game, as a function of FT%, role and margin. Mid-game hack-a-player fouling in Q1-Q3 is included as a separate, rarer component.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.rationale: Late-game attempts form the right tail; whether a player is a target depends on a threshold in FT% for bigs and on being the leading team's ball handler.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.measurement: Per player: attempts in the last 2 minutes of games within 6 points per 100 such minutes (last 3 seasons, shrinkage k=30 minutes); logistic target model with features FT% (below 0.60 flag), ball-handler role, trailing/leading, margin; combine with own-model P(close at 2:00) to give expected additional attempts; update each season after rule changes. Add an early-game component: frequency of intentional away-from-the-ball or hack-a fouls in Q1-Q3 per 100 possessions by opposing coach and target (from play-by-play foul descriptions); outside the last two minutes these are ordinary personal fouls that yield free throws only through the bonus, so they are modelled as extra bonus-state attempts for the targeted low-FT% player.

nba.ft_skill_posterior.label: Free-throw skill posterior (career, three-point, pre-NBA priors)
nba.ft_skill_posterior.mechanism: Make probability is a skill with informative priors for low-sample players.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.rationale: Free-throw percentage over a short sample is noisy; for rookies and low-volume players, three-point percentage and pre-NBA free-throw data improve the estimate.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.measurement: p_hat = (FTM_3y_weighted + a) / (FTA_3y_weighted + a + b), with weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 by season, prior (a, b) from a regression of FT% on 3P% (slope about 0.5 at 100 3PA, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and pre-NBA FT% for rookies, effective prior size 80 attempts; report sd of posterior.

nba.pair_difference_correlation.label: Pair-type correlation of player stat residuals
nba.pair_difference_correlation.mechanism: The correlation between two players' counts differs by pair type (teammates, opponents, separate games) and by stat.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.rationale: The draft says positive correlation through game script, but for teammates the allocation effect is negative; a single sign misprices the difference variance and tie mass.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.measurement: For stat s and pair type, compute the correlation of residuals (after removing player and opponent effects and minutes) over 5 seasons for pairs of similar roles; pool in role-pair cells with shrinkage k=60 games; report the correlation and the implied variance of the difference var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B; produce P(A > B), P(tie), P(B > A) via a bivariate negative-binomial.

nba.series_player_exposure.label: Expected games and minutes exposure over a series
nba.series_player_exposure.mechanism: Series totals depend on the number of games, availability in each, and playoff minutes inflation.
nba.series_player_exposure.rationale: The draft has a series model for the number of games but no link to each player's exposure, including injuries across games and early eliminations.
nba.series_player_exposure.measurement: E[games] = Σ_k P(series length = k) × k; exposure_i = Σ_games P(player i plays game g | series length) × expected minutes_g (playoff inflation factor from role-specific ratio of playoff to regular-season minutes over 10 seasons, shrunk with k=8 players); include injury persistence (probability of playing game g+1 given absent in g about 0.6, estimated); output exposure distribution (mean, sd).

nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.label: Playoff matchup assignment shift (primary defender effect)
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.mechanism: In a series the primary defenders assigned to stars shift counts relative to regular-season rates, adjusted game by game.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.rationale: Regular-season position-based opponent allowances miss the specific defender and the series adaptation. The 5-15% shift magnitude is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (recalled, not estimated).
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.measurement: From tracking matchup data compute for each offensive player the points/assists per 100 possessions guarded by each defender (min 50 possessions) with shrinkage to the defender's overall effect (k=100 possessions); for a series use the expected share of possessions by defender from the last regular-season meeting and playoffs-to-date; shift = Σ share × (matchup rate - baseline); update after each series game with half-life 2 games.

nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.label: Summer League game selection and minutes cap pattern
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.mechanism: Participation and minutes in Summer League depend on draft slot, contract status and team plans, with top picks playing fewer games and veterans resting.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.rationale: Summer League exposure is the main variance of its stat markets, and none of the current inputs gives the probability that a player plays a given game.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.measurement: Per player: P(plays game g) by draft slot bucket (top 5, 6-14, 15-30, second round, undrafted, veteran) from the last 6 Summer Leagues; minutes distribution per game conditional on playing; adjust for team announcements (coded 0/0.5/1) and for back-to-back games; combine to a distribution of games played and total minutes.

nba.dd_category_pair_mix.label: Category-pair decomposition of a player's double-double paths (pts/reb/ast/stl/blk)
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.mechanism: A DD is a union over category pairs; each pair has its own minutes-sensitivity, so the player's probability is a mixture of path-specific probabilities.
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.rationale: A center reaches DD mainly via points+rebounds, a point-forward via points+assists, a rim-protecting big via reb+blk; one scalar 'DD rate' averages over paths whose responses to minutes, blowouts and absences differ, and omits the blocks/steals paths that the contract explicitly counts.
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.measurement: For each player-game with >=12 minutes over current + prior 2 seasons, flag each of 5 categories >=10; compute per-category P(>=10 | minutes bucket 12-20/20-28/28-34/34+) with exponential half-life of 45 games and beta shrinkage toward the position-archetype mean with prior weight 20 games; build pair-path rates P(pair) via joint empirical counts (not products). Output per player: vector of pair-path rates and the share of historical DDs coming from each pair. As-of: only games finished before the tip-off timestamp.

nba.midgame_exit_hazard.label: In-game early-exit hazard (injury, ejection, foul-out, minutes cap)
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.mechanism: Once a player enters the game the contract settles on his stats even if he plays 5 minutes, so truncation by an early exit converts directly into NO.
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.rationale: The rules void only players who are inactive or never take the court; an injury exit after 6 minutes settles NO at near-certainty. The hazard is player-specific (age, injury history, listed status, foul rate) and is distinct from planned blowout minutes cuts.
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, per player-season count games with >=1 minute where minutes < 0.55 x pregame-expected minutes and the exit was not a blowout rest (margin<15 at exit) divided by games entered; classify cause by sub-in/sub-out and injury report. Combine as hazard per 36 minutes with beta(2,40) prior shrinkage and a status multiplier (probable/questionable-return/minutes-restricted) estimated from historical status vintages. As-of: injury report at the latest vintage before tip.

nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.label: Late-game stat-chase and teammate-gifting effect near the 10 threshold
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.mechanism: When a player sits at 9 rebounds or assists in a decided game, teammates and coaches have been observed to funnel the last opportunity, so production near the threshold is not a smooth Poisson continuation.
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.rationale: Garbage-time minutes are normally a pure loss for DD, but stat-chasing partially offsets it; the size is team and coach specific and can be estimated from play-by-play without any market data. It is subtle because it only applies at 8-9 counts with margin >12 late.
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.measurement: From play-by-play, take all instances where a player enters the final 8 game minutes with margin >=12 and a category count of 8 or 9; compute observed rate of reaching 10 per remaining on-court minute divided by that player's baseline per-minute rate in the same category; pool by coach with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (prior weight 25 instances) and report the multiplier. Use as a pregame-fixed multiplier applied only inside the blowout branch.

nba.dd_center_swap_share.label: Rebound/assist share conditional on which co-big or creator shares the floor
nba.dd_center_swap_share.mechanism: Boards and assist chances are split among on-court teammates, so a player's DD path depends on which specific teammates occupy the other four slots in each rotation segment.
nba.dd_center_swap_share.rationale: Season rebound or assist percentage averages over very different lineups; the relevant quantity is the player's share when paired with tonight's expected 5-man units, weighted by expected minutes in each unit.
nba.dd_center_swap_share.measurement: From stint-level data compute the player's TRB% and AST% per lineup context (with each frequent teammate on/off, min 150 possessions) using ridge-regularised on/off coefficients (lambda tuned by rolling CV on prior season); then project tonight's expected minute-weighted lineup mix from rotation history and injury report and sum. Report a minutes-weighted expected board share and assist share with their standard errors.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
