nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.label: Early-exit and foul-out hazard of the scorer (injury, ejection, sixth foul)
nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.mechanism: Points accumulate only while on court and the contract settles on actual points once he enters, so mid-game exits remove the upper tail entirely.
nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.rationale: Average minutes hide a distribution with a point mass at early departure; for older or injury-prone scorers and foul-prone drivers it is several percent per game and it is not captured by status labels alone.
nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.measurement: From box score and play-by-play, per player-season: share of games entered with minutes < 0.55 x pregame expected minutes and a non-blowout exit, plus share ending by sixth foul or ejection; beta(2,40) shrinkage to a position prior, 60-game half-life; multiply by a status factor for Questionable/Probable/returning-from-injury estimated from archived report vintages. Feeds a mixture weight for the short-minutes branch.

nba.usage_allocation_model.label: Lineup-conditional shot-attempt allocation model for tonight's expected on-court unit
nba.usage_allocation_model.mechanism: Team attempts are a roughly fixed pie divided among the five on court according to creation roles, so a scorer's share is a function of the whole unit, not just whether one named teammate is out.
nba.usage_allocation_model.rationale: With/without splits rest on tiny samples and ignore that replacing a creator by a catch-and-shoot wing shifts shots differently than replacing him by another creator; an allocation model with role types generalises across rosters.
nba.usage_allocation_model.measurement: Fit a Dirichlet-multinomial (or softmax) model of FGA+0.44*FTA+TOV shares among the five on-court players using stint data, with player creation archetype, on-ball minutes share and prior-season usage as features; ridge-regularised, 2-season window with 200-game half-life; predict tonight's shares for the projected unit set (weighted by expected minutes per unit) and report mean and standard error. As-of: injury report at last vintage.

nba.cross_player_points_dependence.label: Dependence of points across players (teammates, opponents, same player multi-stat)
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.mechanism: Teammates compete for the same possessions (negative within team conditional on total) while all players share pace and shooting variance of the game (positive across teams), which sets joint-event probabilities.
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.rationale: Head-to-head, combined-stat and points-leader products are functions of the joint law of several players' points; marginals alone give wrong answers, e.g. two opponent stars' point difference has a variance depending on the sign of their correlation.
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.measurement: Estimate pairwise correlations of residual points (actual minus minutes-conditional expectation) for same-team and opposite-team pairs over a 2-season window with Fisher-z shrinkage toward position-pair prior (weight 40 games); also correlation of a player's points with his own rebounds+assists residuals for PRA/PR/PA products. Cross-team pairs typically near +0.1 via pace; same-team pairs typically negative.

nba.points_upper_tail_rate.label: Player-specific upper-tail frequency of points given full-minutes games (ceiling-game rate)
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.mechanism: Scoring has a heavier right tail than a negative binomial fit to the mean implies because hot shooting, FT surges and OT stack; the cubic escalator weights this tail heavily.
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.rationale: The scalar escalator pays (y/50)^3 so its expected value is dominated by 35+ outcomes; a model calibrated to the mean misprices it, and the 30+/40+ rungs depend on the same tail.
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.measurement: For each player estimate exceedance probabilities P(pts >= 1.4m), P(pts >= 1.7m) and P(pts>=2.0m) where m is the minutes-conditional mean, on games with >=30 minutes over a 3-season window; fit a generalised-Pareto above the 85th percentile of residuals with shape shrunk to a league-wide value (prior weight 60 exceedances). Output the tail index and exceedance rates.

nba.player_xpts_per_shot.label: Shot-level expected points per attempt for the player vs tonight's defense
nba.player_xpts_per_shot.mechanism: Points per attempt is a function of shot type and location (rim, midrange, corner and above-the-break three, action type) and the shooter's finishing talent, so team zone averages mix very different shooters.
nba.player_xpts_per_shot.rationale: Opponent zone-allowed tables ignore who takes the shots; a pull-up scorer vs drop coverage and a roll man vs switching differ by large amounts and these are mostly knowable pregame.
nba.player_xpts_per_shot.measurement: From shot-level data estimate a hierarchical model of make probability by player x shot zone x action type (shotchartdetail location, ACTION_TYPE, SHOT_TYPE and SHOT_DISTANCE fields) with beta priors (rim prior weight 150 FGA, three prior weight 750 FGA, midrange 300); multiply by opponent's allowed frequency/quality for each shot type (opponent-adjusted by league mean) to get predicted points per shot; sum over projected attempts by type. As-of: shots finished before tip-off. Closest-defender distance is not part of the base model; an optional season-level adjustment may use aggregate defender-distance bins from the tracking dashboards (not crossed with location), pending pp-defender-distance.

nba.combo_component_marginals.label: Rebound and assist component marginals and their dependence with points (for PRA, PR, PA contracts)
nba.combo_component_marginals.mechanism: A combined points+rebounds+assists count is the sum of three correlated components, each with its own minutes-scaled rate, so the ladder probability needs marginal rebound and assist models and their residual dependence with points, not the points model alone.
nba.combo_component_marginals.rationale: KXNBAPRA, KXNBAPR, KXNBAPA and KXNBAH2HPRA settle on sums of components. For a big man the rebound share is worth as much as the scoring, for a guard the assist share is, and the variance of the sum depends on whether components are positively tied through minutes or traded off through usage (a ball-dominant guard scoring more usually assists less). Modelling only points and adding a constant for the other components understates the spread of the sum, which moves high rungs the most.
nba.combo_component_marginals.measurement: For each player build minutes-scaled rates for rebounds and assists: rate_k = (sum_over_games w_g * k_g + 500 * prior_rate_k) / (sum_over_games w_g * min_g + 500), with exponential game weights w_g (half-life 40 games) and a position-group prior rate (500 minutes of prior weight is a placeholder to be fitted). Component counts given minutes are negative binomial with dispersion fitted by position group. Dependence: residuals (actual minus minutes-conditional expectation) for points, rebounds and assists over a 2-season window, correlation matrix shrunk by Fisher-z toward the position-group prior (weight 40 games), joined with a Gaussian copula over the three marginals. Output is the distribution of P+R+A, P+R and P+A in each minutes scenario, mixed by the minutes scenario weights. Tonight's rebound and assist drivers (nba.reb_chances, nba.pot_ast, nba.rebound_pool, teammate absences) enter as multipliers on rate_k and are defined in the player_rebounds and player_milestones records of this file. As-of: games completed before tipoff.
free_sources: nba_api boxscore endpoints (player-game rebounds, assists, minutes)

nba.creditable_rebound_pool.label: Player-creditable rebound pool: misses net of team rebounds and dead-ball leakage
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.mechanism: Official player rebounds exclude team rebounds (shot-clock violations, balls out of bounds, first free-throw misses of a pair), so the pool a player can be credited from is smaller than total misses and varies by game flow.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.rationale: A pool built from field-goal misses alone overstates supply when games have many foul-heavy trips, where missed first free throws and dead-ball team rebounds produce no player rebound; the leakage share is hypothesised to be of the order of 6-10% of misses (unverified, to be estimated from team rebound counts; see pr-leakage-source) and should vary with foul rate.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.measurement: For each team-game: creditable_pool = FG misses + live FT misses (last free throw of a trip) - (team rebounds + out-of-bounds recoveries); estimate team-level leakage ratio by regressing team rebounds on FG misses, FT trips and out-of-bounds counts over 2 seasons with 80-game half-life; project tonight's pool as projected combined misses (ratings and shot-quality based, not market totals) times (1 - projected leakage). Leakage uses opponent foul rate and arena (scorer) effect.
free_sources: nba_api team box scores (reb, oreb, dreb, team reb)

nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.label: Rebound percentage conditional on specific frontcourt pairings (ridge on/off)
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.mechanism: A big's share of available boards depends on which other rebounders share the floor in each stint; the same player has very different shares beside a stretch four vs a second center.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.rationale: Season TRB% averages over pairings; because rotation patterns change with injury news, what matters is the expected minute-weighted mix of tonight's pairings, which is predictable pregame once availability is known.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.measurement: From stint data, regress player TRB% on indicator vectors of teammates on court (ridge, lambda chosen by rolling-origin CV on previous season, minimum 150 possessions per pair) with opponent offensive-rebounding strength as a covariate; project tonight's stint mix = rotation minutes by lineup weighted by injury-conditioned availability; output expected share and its standard error. DREB% and OREB% estimated separately because OREB is lineup-sensitive.

nba.team_glass_strategy.label: Offensive-glass crash rate versus transition-defense tradeoff of each team and coach
nba.team_glass_strategy.mechanism: Coaches choose how many players crash the offensive boards; heavy crashing raises OREB for bigs and lowers the opponent's DREB share while increasing transition possessions for opponents.
nba.team_glass_strategy.rationale: Crash policy is a team trait that is persistent across seasons within a coach, and it changes both rebound counts and pace; it is not recoverable from rebound pool or pace alone.
nba.team_glass_strategy.measurement: Compute per team-season OREB% and opponent transition points per possession after offensive rebounds (from play-by-play possession types) with 70-game half-life and coach-tenure reset; build matchup term = own crash rate x opponent weakness against crashing (opponent's DREB% minus expected from size) and report separately for OREB and DREB attributable to the player's position.

nba.big_exit_protection_state.label: Big-man early-exit and first-half-only participation hazard, mapped to protected-contract voiding
nba.big_exit_protection_state.mechanism: Protected rebound contracts refund any player who enters in the first half but does not enter after halftime (including overtime), whatever the cause: injury or foul-out, ejection, or a coach resting him for the whole second half of a lopsided game.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.rationale: In standard contracts an early exit settles NO; in protected series the same event refunds at a pre-tip fair price, so the same underlying hazard has opposite market consequences and must be tracked separately for the two forms. Blowout-driven second-half rest is the cause most likely to be missed: a bench big who played 6 first-half minutes in a game that is 25 points at halftime is refunded, so the refund branch also depends on the margin path.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.measurement: Per player-season, estimate P(minutes in 2H+OT = 0 | entered 1H) and P(exit before 12 total minutes) from play-by-play with beta(2,40) shrinkage and a status multiplier; output separately, by cause (injury or ejection, foul-out, blowout rest of the whole second half): hazard of 'plays only first half' (protected refund branch) and 'exits early without refund'. The blowout-rest cause is estimated as P(no second-half minutes | entered 1H, halftime margin bin) and is driven by nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (rare for starters, common for deep-bench bigs). As-of: injury report vintage.

nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.label: Hierarchical make probability by shot type (catch-and-shoot vs pull-up) and defender openness
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.mechanism: Make probability depends on shot context more than on a single season 3P%, so talent should be estimated per context and recombined with tonight's expected context mix.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.rationale: Overall 3P% averages over open catch-and-shoot threes (about 38%) and tightly contested pull-ups (about 31%); a shooter's attempt mix changes with teammates and opposing closeouts, so the make probability changes even with fixed talent.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.measurement: Base model (public per-shot data): beta-binomial hierarchy on made/attempted by shot zone (corner, above the break) x pull-up flag from shotchartdetail ACTION_TYPE and SHOT_ZONE fields over 3 seasons, league-cell mean as prior with prior weight 250 attempts per cell, partial pooling by player, recent-season weight 0.5 per year. Optional refinement if the tracking dashboards are confirmed (p3-defender-distance): aggregate catch-and-shoot versus pull-up and closest-defender bins (wide open 6+ ft, open 4-6, tight under 4) as separate multiplicative adjustments, not a crossed cell, because the dashboards are not per-shot. Combine with tonight's predicted context mix from shot-creation role and opponent openness allowed. Output a single p3 with credible interval. As-of: shots finished before tip.

nba.three_att_script_elasticity.label: Elasticity of a shooter's three-point attempt rate to score margin and quarter
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.mechanism: Trailing teams take more threes late and leading teams run clock and bench shooters, so 3PA per minute is a function of the margin path, not a constant.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.rationale: Blowout dynamics cut starters but raise bench shooters' attempts; a close fourth quarter raises volume for closers; the sign differs between roles, so a single 'blowout' penalty misprices spot-up wings and bench shooters.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.measurement: From play-by-play estimate per player 3PA per minute in margin bins (<-12, -12..-5, -5..+5, +5..+12, >+12) by quarter, with empirical-Bayes shrinkage to role-archetype bins (prior weight 120 minutes per bin); combine with the projected distribution of margin paths from team ratings (not the spread). Output expected 3PA integrating over the margin-path distribution and minutes mixture.

nba.assisted_three_passer_map.label: Share of shooter's made threes assisted by each teammate (passer dependence)
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.mechanism: A catch-and-shoot three requires a passer; the loss of a particular creator removes a specific fraction of assisted looks, with replacement playmakers delivering fewer.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.rationale: Absence adjustments built from with/without splits ignore that dependence is concentrated in a few passers; in many pairs one creator generates 30-40% of a shooter's threes, so his absence matters far more than other absences.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.measurement: From play-by-play assists, compute for each shooter the share of made+missed assisted threes by passer over 2 seasons (shrink shares to team-average share by prior weight 40 attempts); expected change in attempts = sum over passers of share x P(passer out) x (1 - replacement factor), replacement factor estimated from games the passer missed (default 0.65). As-of: injury report vintage.

nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.label: Opponent's rate of open and wide-open three-point attempts allowed (closeout quality)
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.mechanism: A defense's effect on a shooter's threes shows up in the proportion of attempts that are open, which is a scheme trait and more persistent than opponent 3P% allowed.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.rationale: Opponent 3P% allowed mixes luck with scheme; the open-attempt share allowed and the opponent's volume allowed by shot type are stable within a season and map directly to a shooter's catch-and-shoot context.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.measurement: From team-level aggregate defense dashboards (closest-defender bins, one row per team and date window, not per-shot; window set by a DateTo filter to games before tip) compute per defense the percentage of opponent threes taken with closest defender >= 4 ft (wide open) and 2-4 ft (open), the corner share allowed, and opponent 3PA allowed per 100 possessions; 60-game half-life, shrink to league mean with prior weight 40 games; match against the shooter's tonight's expected cell mix.
free_sources: nba_api defense dashboards by closest defender

nba.quarter_unit_projection.label: Per-quarter expected on-court units and their projected net/offensive rating
nba.quarter_unit_projection.mechanism: Each quarter's scoring is the possession-weighted sum of ratings of the specific five-man units on the floor; coaches' stagger patterns make Q2 and Q4 weak or strong depending on who is available.
nba.quarter_unit_projection.rationale: Full-game ratings average over rotation; Q2 often features bench units with one starter, while Q1 and Q3 start with the best five. Because rotation patterns are predictable from coach tenure and are altered by injuries, a projection by quarter is a pregame-computable improvement over team ratings.
nba.quarter_unit_projection.measurement: For each team, build per-quarter minute-share matrix (player x quarter) from last 30 games with 15-game half-life, conditioned on starters confirmed and injury vintages; map to expected unit compositions; apply ridge-regularised lineup/player on-off ratings (lambda tuned by rolling CV) to compute expected points per 100 possessions in each quarter; adjust for opponent unit by the same method. Output: expected team points and margin per quarter with standard errors.

nba.period_margin_pmf.label: Empirical period-margin and period-total probability mass functions (ties, half-point cut points)
nba.period_margin_pmf.mechanism: Quarter margins are small integers with a sizeable mass at zero and at +/-1..3; winner, spread and total contracts cut this discrete distribution at specific points, so pmf shape (not only mean and sd) sets the probability.
nba.period_margin_pmf.rationale: A Gaussian approximation misprices tie mass (about 4-6% per quarter) and the probability of exceeding a half-point strike; the shape depends on pace (lower-possession periods have fewer scoring events) and on variance of the team-pair.
nba.period_margin_pmf.measurement: From all games in 5 seasons compute standardized period margin and total (actual minus rating-based expectation, built without market lines), fit a discrete mixture (Skellam-like with pace-dependent variance and a small-excess-kurtosis component) per period type (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, 1H, 2H-with-OT) via maximum likelihood with a team-pair variance covariate; report pmf at integer margins within +/-25 and the tie probability by expected pace tercile.

nba.period_foul_bonus_state.label: Team-foul and bonus-state exposure per period (foul reset each quarter, end-of-period fouling)
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.mechanism: Team fouls reset each quarter, so the shape of free-throw production within a period depends on when a team reaches the penalty, and Q4 end-of-period fouling adds free throws that distort Q4 totals and margins.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.rationale: Free-throw volume per period differs from per-game rates because bonus onset is quarter-specific; crews that call more early fouls bring forward bonus situations in Q1/Q3, which can change period totals by 2-3 points; the effect is partly predictable from crew and team foul rates.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.measurement: Compute team FTA per quarter and fouls per quarter from play-by-play over 2 seasons with 60-game half-life; estimate crew and team coefficients on quarter FTA via mixed model; project expected time-to-bonus in each quarter and expected FTA by period for tonight's matchup and crew; output expected FT points by period. As-of: crew assignment (announced game day) and team rates.

nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.label: Coach-specific second-half and Q3 adjustment effect (Q3 efficiency minus game baseline)
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.mechanism: After halftime coaches adjust schemes and starters re-enter, so Q3 scoring is not an average of Q1 and Q2 and certain coaches systematically outscore their baseline in Q3.
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.rationale: Q3 and Q1 both start with starters but have different information sets; evidence of Q3 effects by coach is plausible but noisy; the quantity matters for Q3 winner/spread/total and for the 2H markets, and interacts with lead size.
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.measurement: For each coach-team-season compute Q3 net rating minus first-half net rating regressed on margin at halftime and minutes played by starters in the first half; empirical-Bayes shrink across coaches (variance component estimated by method of moments) so that individual coach effects are heavily shrunk (typical shrinkage 80-90%); apply only when the coach is unchanged. As-of: games before tip.

nba.period_possession_split.label: Possessions by quarter and team pace profile (fast early, slower late in lopsided games)
nba.period_possession_split.mechanism: Possessions per quarter vary by period (fast Q1, slower Q4 in decided games) and each coach has a pace style, so period totals scale with a period-specific possession count.
nba.period_possession_split.rationale: Applying game pace to a quarter overstates Q4 possessions in blowouts and understates Q1 for fast starters; the possession count times PPP is the correct decomposition for totals and team totals.
nba.period_possession_split.measurement: From play-by-play compute possessions per quarter per team with the standard possession formula (FGA - OREB + TOV + 0.44 FTA) by period for the last 2 seasons with 50-game half-life; model matchup period pace as weighted geometric mean with a slow-team weight of about 0.55 (estimate by regression); condition Q4 on pregame blowout-probability tercile. Output expected possessions per period and sd.
free_sources: nba_api box scores by period / PBP

nba.first_passage_race_table.label: Empirical race-to-N first-passage table by N, opening possession and early-game rating gap
nba.first_passage_race_table.mechanism: First-to-N is a first-passage problem on two alternating-possession scoring processes with lumpy increments; the answer depends on N, who has the ball first and the early-game scoring rate gap.
nba.first_passage_race_table.rationale: Treating the race as two independent Poisson clocks mispredicts because possessions alternate and scores come in 1-3 point lumps; the first-possession advantage is hypothesised to be about half a possession (unverified) and its relative value shrinks with N, so a table by N is needed. Scope: single-game race-to-N only; it does not describe a season-long first-to-threshold contract.
nba.first_passage_race_table.measurement: From 5 seasons of play-by-play compute for each game and each N in {5,10,15,20,25,30} which team reached N first, whether that team had the opening possession and the starters' first-stint net rating gap; fit logistic regressions per N with covariates (opening possession, rating gap, home) and ridge shrinkage; output P(win race) with standard errors. Rating gap uses the first-stint rating below, not full-game rating.

nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.label: Starting-five first-stint offensive and defensive rating and scoring-event mix
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.mechanism: The race is decided in the first 4-8 minutes by the starters, whose joint rating differs from season team rating and depends on the exact five.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.rationale: Season team ratings average starters and bench; a starter-specific, first-stint rating (with set plays, shot mix and turnover rate) is the relevant strength and changes immediately if one starter is replaced.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.measurement: For each team compute points per 100 possessions and per-possession scoring-event distribution (0,1,2,3 points) for the first 8 minutes of games using the modal starting five over last 60 games (half-life 30 games), shrink to the team's full-game rating with prior weight 400 possessions; when tonight's starters differ, recompute via player-level on/off ridge ratings. As-of: starters confirmation time.

nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.label: Historical probability of being the game's top scorer by team scoring rank and usage gap
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.mechanism: The leader is the maximum of about 20 players' points, concentrated among each team's top two or three scorers; the share a player has as leader depends on the gap in expected points to the nearest rivals, not on his own mean.
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.rationale: Treating each player's points as independent normals overstates the chance of the second option and ignores that teammates' points are negatively correlated given team total; empirical leader shares by rank and gap calibrate the max-of-correlated-variables model.
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.measurement: From 5 seasons of box scores compute for every player-game his rank among teammates by pregame expected points, the gap to the top rival in expected points, minutes and the indicator of leading both teams in points (with tie handling set per rule); fit a conditional logit on gap, team scoring concentration and OT; output P(leader) by rank-gap cell with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (prior weight 80 games per cell).

nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.label: Correlation of scoring between a team's top scorers and across the two teams
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.mechanism: Teammates split a roughly fixed number of shots so a big night for one lowers the other, while both teams share pace and officiating; this sets the covariance structure of the maximum.
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.rationale: Leader probability depends on the joint distribution: if two stars were positively correlated, the max would be less spread out than if negatively correlated; both are estimable from box scores.
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.measurement: Estimate residual-points correlation (actual minus minutes-conditional expectation) for each team's top-3 scorer pairs and for cross-team top-scorer pairs over 2 seasons using Fisher-z shrinkage to a league pair-type prior (prior weight 40 games); condition on co-star availability. Output a covariance matrix over the candidate set.

nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.label: Preseason team prior from minutes-weighted roster impact with aging curves and continuity
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.mechanism: A team's true strength before and early in the season is a function of who is on the roster, how those players age, and how much of last year's unit returns; this prior dominates for the first 20-30 games.
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.rationale: With about ten games played, the 2026-27 rating is mostly the prior; building it from last season's team rating ignores offseason roster churn, aging and rookie contributions, and the error of the prior sets the uncertainty of every futures contract.
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.measurement: Prior team rating = sum over projected rotation of (expected minutes share x player impact projection), where projection = last-two-season blended impact (weights 0.6/0.3/0.1 over 3 seasons) + aging adjustment by age bucket (estimated from historical year-over-year change; roughly +1.0/-0.3/-1.0 per 100 possessions at ages 22/28/33) + continuity adjustment (minutes-weighted share of returning players, coefficient estimated by backtest); shrink to league mean by sd of prior error estimated from 10 historical seasons; report mean and sd. As-of: before opening night and updated at each roster transaction.
free_sources: EPM / RAPM published by Dunks&Threes or similar

nba.rating_update_gain.label: In-season rating update gain and posterior sd (how fast current results override the prior)
nba.rating_update_gain.mechanism: True team strength is updated game by game with weight given by signal-to-noise; the gain declines with games played, and calibrating it by backtest sets how fast futures should move.
nba.rating_update_gain.rationale: A rating that overweights early results (10 games) swings futures; under-weighting leaves stale priors. The right gain is estimated from past seasons and depends on whether margin or win/loss is used and on roster stability.
nba.rating_update_gain.measurement: Backtest across the last 15 seasons: regress end-of-season margin per game on preseason prior and games-played-weighted current margin; solve for optimal weight w(n) as a function of games played n (expect w near 0.2 at n=10, 0.5 at n=40); posterior sd of true rating = sqrt(prior_var x (1-w)); use margin of victory capped at 15 and garbage-time excluded. As-of: all games before the as-of date.

nba.tiebreak_ledger.label: Head-to-head, division and conference record ledger for tiebreaker evaluation
nba.tiebreak_ledger.mechanism: Seeds and division winners are decided by the league's tiebreak hierarchy (head-to-head, division winner, conference record and so on), so exact ties are resolved by information that accumulates over the season.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.rationale: Simulating only win totals misses the probability that a tie is broken in a team's favor; at seed boundaries (6th vs 7th, 10th vs 11th, play-in cutoff) a tie occurs in about 8-15% of final standings and the tiebreak ledger is partly known before the season ends.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.measurement: For each team pair compute season-to-date head-to-head wins/losses and remaining games, division record, conference record and record vs playoff teams, updated nightly from game results; in the simulation, apply the official tiebreak procedure (stored as code from league rules) to simulated ties and output P(win tie) by pair. As-of: nightly after final scores.

nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.label: Time-resolved probability that each rotation star is healthy for each playoff round
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.mechanism: Title and conference odds are convex in star availability, and the relevant availability is in April-June, not the regular-season games-missed average.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.rationale: Games-missed expectations average over a season; the quantity that matters for round-reach contracts is the probability of being healthy at tip of each playoff series, which depends on current injury state, history, age and minutes load.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.measurement: For each player in the top-3 of each contender estimate a hazard model for an injury ending availability (survival model by age, previous-season games missed, minutes per game, current injury status) fitted on 10 seasons of injury data; output P(healthy at playoff start), P(healthy for round k) conditional on being healthy at the start; combine with team-level strength loss from the player's absence (impact x minutes share). As-of: injury report vintage.

nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.label: Probability a given player wins Finals/Conference Finals MVP conditional on his team winning the series
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.mechanism: Award contracts are conditional on the team winning and then on voter choice among its players, which follows stat shares and narrative in the series.
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.rationale: Finals MVP of a champion usually goes to the top scorer or best player of the series, with media voters weighing series scoring, efficiency and team role; P(player MVP) = P(team wins) x P(player chosen | team wins) and the second factor can be estimated from past award results.
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.measurement: From 20 seasons of Finals and Conference Finals results compute for each champion's top-3 players the share of MVP awards by rank in series points, by pre-series team star ranking and by minutes share; fit a conditional logit on pre-series expected points rank and best-player indicator (pre-series BPM rank), regularised; output P(MVP | team wins) by player. Combine with series win probability from the series model. As-of: before series start (updated per game).

nba.finals_viewership_drivers.label: Finals viewership drivers: market sizes, star power, series length and Game 7 incidence
nba.finals_viewership_drivers.mechanism: A viewership threshold contract depends on the matchup's audience size (markets, stars), series length and number of games, and the broadcast measurement method rather than on team strength alone.
nba.finals_viewership_drivers.rationale: KXNBAFINALSVIEWER and KXNBAFINALSVIEWERGAME7 settle on audience counts; these are functions of which teams reach the Finals, how many games are played and the rating baselines of past years; they are not outcomes of basketball production but of audiences.
nba.finals_viewership_drivers.measurement: Regress average Finals viewership on the log combined TV market size of the two teams, a star-power index (number of all-NBA/All-Star players), series length and prior-year trend over 15 seasons (use published Nielsen figures as released by the broadcaster); add year effects for measurement changes (out-of-home viewing, streaming) and forecast with a prediction interval. As-of: before the Finals, updated by conference-finals outcomes.
free_sources: Sports Media Watch / press releases of Nielsen ratings (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for completeness)

nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.label: Distribution of the league-longest win streak and the number of tied teams (1/N payout) from game-level simulation
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.mechanism: The league-longest streak is the maximum over 30 teams of the longest run of consecutive wins in each team's sequence, so a 'longest streak' contract depends on every team's game-by-game win probabilities, their serial dependence, and the chance that two or more teams share the maximum and split the payout.
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.rationale: KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK pays $1/N to each of N teams tied for the longest streak and only regular-season games (Cup games before the final included) count, so the value for one team is P(it holds the maximum) times E[1/N | it does]. Strengths matter through a convex path: the best team is not only more likely to have a long run but also faces a different set of opponents and rest games, and common rating shocks make streaks cluster in time and in teams. Ignoring ties overstates the value of a favourite when two strong teams reach the same length.
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.measurement: Simulate 20000 seasons from nba.standings_sim: draw team ratings from the posterior (rating uncertainty common across a team's games), form each game's win probability from rating difference, home court and rest, then record each team's longest run (a streak carrying over the Cup group stage and counting Cup knockout games before the final, excluding the final, play-in and playoffs). For each team report P(team has the strict maximum), P(team is in the tied set), the distribution of N and E[payout] = E[floor(100/N)/100 * 1{team in the tied set}]. Calibrate the serial dependence by comparing simulated run-length distributions with the last 15 seasons of real streak lengths (league-longest streak and its tie frequency). As-of: games completed to date, with the current run for each team carried in.
free_sources: nba_api leaguegamelog (game results by team and date)

nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.label: Voting-panel and nominee model for award contracts, including the probability of multiple co-winners
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.mechanism: Award contracts such as the Social Justice Champion, Finals MVP, conference finals MVP and Cup All-Tournament selections are decided by a panel or vote among nominees, not by team simulation, so the relevant quantities are the nominee set, the historical winner profile and the chance of several winners.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.rationale: For KXNBASJC the sampled rules split the payout $1/N among multiple awardees, so P(multiple winners) and the winner's profile (community work and nominee status) matter more than basketball production. For Finals and conference finals MVPs the winner is chosen from the winning team after the series by a panel, so the team simulation only gives the first factor. Panels are small, so narrative and series stats can dominate and the winner is a discrete choice among a few candidates.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.measurement: Build an award history table (at least 15 seasons) of nominees or finalists, winner(s) and the number of awardees. Fit a conditional logit for P(winner | nominee) on prior finalist or winner status, team success, and for series MVPs on series points rank and best-player indicator, with ridge regularisation and a prior weight of 10 award-years. Estimate P(more than one awardee) as the historical frequency with a beta(1,10) prior, and the expected payout as P(win) x E[1/N | win] rounded down to the cent. For game-based MVPs multiply by P(team wins the series) from nba.series_model. As-of: before announcement, updated when finalists are published.
free_sources: NBA.com award announcements and press releases

nba.stat_rate_posterior.label: Shrunk posterior of a player's true per-game stat rate given games to date and preseason projection
nba.stat_rate_posterior.mechanism: A season-long average or leader race depends on the player's true rate, which is a weighted combination of the preseason projection and the noisy to-date average.
nba.stat_rate_posterior.rationale: Early-season averages overstate hot starts; the weight on results needs to be calibrated per statistic (scoring is more stable than rebounding and assists), and the posterior variance determines how much the leader gap is worth.
nba.stat_rate_posterior.measurement: Prior mean = preseason projection (last-two-season blend with aging adjustment); weights by stat: n_prior of about 25 games for points, 35 for rebounds, 40 for assists (these three values are placeholders, not fitted estimates; they must be estimated by a backtest of ten seasons); posterior mean = (n_prior x prior + n x observed)/(n_prior + n) with minutes-conditional adjustment; posterior sd = sqrt(per-game variance/(n_prior + n)). As-of: games to date.

nba.qualification_probability.label: Probability a candidate meets the contract's qualification rule (games, minutes, or none)
nba.qualification_probability.mechanism: Leader and award-like markets require a minimum number of games or minutes; a player's chance depends on the distribution of games played and on strategic rest near the threshold.
nba.qualification_probability.rationale: A scoring leader who misses 25 games might be disqualified under a minimum-games rule or still counted if the rule says qualification thresholds do not apply; this is a cliff in the payoff and varies by contract.
nba.qualification_probability.measurement: For each candidate compute P(games_played >= G_min) where G_min is read from the contract (or 0 if 'qualification thresholds do not apply'): games played = games to date + Binomial-like process over remaining games with per-game availability from an injury-hazard model and a load-management multiplier for players >30 or with a history of rest; record probability and the conditional leader probability given qualification; update after every game.

nba.streak_hit_persistence.label: Game-to-game persistence of threshold hits and streak-break hazard (DNP, rest, matchup)
nba.streak_hit_persistence.mechanism: A streak of N games meeting a threshold is a run-length process whose per-game hit probability varies with minutes and rest and which is broken by any DNP or rest night.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.rationale: Treating hits as independent with the season-average rate understates both streak and break risk; minutes and rest dependencies create positive autocorrelation within a stretch, and the specific rule (whether inactive games break the streak) changes everything.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.measurement: For each player estimate a logistic model of threshold hit on minutes projection, rest days, opponent defensive rating and lag-1 hit (to capture persistence beyond minutes) over a 3-season window; compute probability of a run of length at least N via a Markov chain with state = current run length and per-game hit probability from the model; add break hazard per game from injury/rest model. Adjust for the rule on inactive games (counts as break, skip, or void).

nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.label: Dependence between teams' records via head-to-head games and conference schedule overlap
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.mechanism: Records of contending teams are not independent: when two top teams play each other, one gains what the other loses, and shared opponents create correlation in schedule luck.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.rationale: Best-record and most-wins markets are about the maximum over teams, so the covariance of wins across teams matters; ignoring head-to-head linkage and common opponents misstates the extreme's distribution.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.measurement: From the remaining schedule compute pairwise numbers of head-to-head games and common-opponent overlap; in the simulation draw correlated team-strength shocks and enforce zero-sum head-to-head results; estimate the covariance of final win totals across the top-8 contenders by simulation; output distribution of the maximum and the probability of ties (tie handling per rule). As-of: nightly.

nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.label: Draft lottery combinatorial odds by pre-lottery rank, including ties and the four-pick rule
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.mechanism: Pick position for non-playoff teams is a random draw with fixed odds by rank (worst three teams each 14.0% for the top pick, no team falling more than four slots, under the current lottery rules (to be re-confirmed for the draft year)), so draft-position contracts reduce to rank odds times a rank distribution.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.rationale: Draft top-3/top-5/top-10 contracts are decided by the lottery, which is a known combinatorial mechanism; the uncertainty is the pre-lottery rank (final record, ties, coin flips) and the team's pick ownership, not the draw itself.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.measurement: Encode the current lottery's 1,000 (or 14 x ...) combination allocation by rank 1-14, compute exact P(pick k | rank r) for k=1..14 (including the rule that teams cannot fall more than 4 positions and ties in record are broken by random drawing before the lottery); combine with the simulated distribution of final regular-season ranks from the standings simulation (include play-in losers) to get P(top-3 pick | team). As-of: nightly; rules versioned by draft year.

nba.pick_ownership_ledger.label: Pick ownership, swap and protection ledger (who holds each first-round pick and conditions)
nba.pick_ownership_ledger.mechanism: A team's lottery position and a player's draft slot depend on who owns the pick, on swaps (the better of two picks) and on protections that roll or convey only above a rank.
nba.pick_ownership_ledger.rationale: Contracts on a team's draft position or a player's slot are about picks, which may be owned by another team, swapped or protected; a model based on the team's own record will misattribute the outcome.
nba.pick_ownership_ledger.measurement: Build a table by draft year with (original team, current owner, protection threshold (e.g. top-8 protected), swap condition, rollover year, second-round pick conveyance) from public transaction records; in simulation, determine each pick's final owner and slot after draw; maintain nightly updates for trades; validate against NBA.com list of draft picks. As-of: transaction dates.

nba.play_in_path_model.label: Play-in bracket path probabilities given pre-play-in seed and relative strength
nba.play_in_path_model.mechanism: The play-in tournament maps seeds 7-10 to final seeds 7 and 8 through a fixed bracket, so the playoff qualification and the post-play-in seed differ from the regular-season seed; Kalshi's seed contracts are measured before the play-in.
nba.play_in_path_model.rationale: KXNBASEEDOU resolves on the regular-season seed before the play-in while qualification/play-in series depend on play-in outcomes; the same team has different probabilities for 'seed 8 or better' depending on which definition applies.
nba.play_in_path_model.measurement: Encode the bracket (7v8 winner gets the 7 seed; 9v10 loser is out; loser of 7v8 plays winner of 9v10 for the 8 seed), compute per-game win probabilities with home-court from team ratings and rest, and convolve to P(final seed 7, 8, out | pre-play-in seed, opponents); estimate the distribution of opponents from the standings simulation. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.

nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.label: Distribution of the number of home playoff games by seed and path
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.mechanism: A team's total home playoff games is the sum over rounds of home games in each series, which depend on home-court status (seed), series length and advancement.
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.rationale: KXNBAPLAYOFFHOMEGAMES and KXNBAPLAYOFFHOST count games rather than winners; probability mass depends on the series-length distribution (4-7 games) and on losing in an early round with few home games.
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.measurement: For each team and round compute P(reach round) from the bracket simulation, P(home-court) from the seed comparison, and the distribution of home games in a series given length and home status (2-2-1-1-1: 4,3,3,2 or 2 for lower seed... enumerate); convolve across rounds into a pmf of total home games; produce two variants of the pmf, one counting play-in home games and one excluding them, because the sampled text does not say which applies (sc-titleonly); the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern is the NBA best-of-seven format in every round. As-of: nightly during playoffs.
free_sources: Computed from the series model and NBA schedule format

nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.label: Cup group standings state with point-differential tiebreak and remaining-games simulation
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.mechanism: Cup group qualifiers are decided by group record then tiebreakers (head-to-head, point differential and so on), so the state is a table with a margin component that rewards running up scores in some games.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.rationale: Group-winner and qualifier contracts depend on remaining games, but also on margin of victory in each game because the point-differential tiebreak influences outcomes; a win/loss-only simulation misses this.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.measurement: From the Cup schedule compute standings, point differential and head-to-head results to date; simulate the remaining group games with margin distributions from team ratings (sd about 13 points per game) and apply the official group tiebreak order and wildcard rule to produce P(group winner), P(qualifier by wildcard); update after each Cup game. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.

nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.label: Per-player playoff triple-double rate given expected games and minutes
nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.mechanism: A playoff triple-double contract is an at-least-one-event over the playoffs; probability depends on the few players with triple-double production, the expected number of playoff games each plays and their playoff minutes.
nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.rationale: KXNBAPLAYOFF3D cannot be priced from regular-season rates alone: minutes rise for stars, games depend on series length and advancement, and triple-double rate per game is concentrated in a handful of high-assist bigs and guards.
nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.measurement: For each candidate compute P(triple-double | game) from regular-season rate adjusted by playoff minutes factor (starters about +2 to +4 minutes) with shrinkage to a role prior (weight 20 games); expected games from the bracket simulation as a distribution; P(at least one TD in playoffs) = 1 - E[(1-p)^G]; aggregate across candidates with correlations through team advancement. As-of: nightly.

nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.label: Market-free prospect draft-slot probability model from public boards, measurables and team needs
nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.mechanism: Player-slot draft contracts (top 5, top 10, top 20 and so on) need the probability that a named prospect is selected at or before a slot, which is the product of the team's pick position (from the lottery and ownership layers) and a ranked-choice model of who each team takes.
nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.rationale: The catalog input nba.draft_board mixes a public consensus rank with 'the market may lead the public mocks', so it can smuggle a price into the model. A market-free version uses only non-price information: aggregated public big boards and mocks (weighted by their past accuracy), combine and workout measurables, age and team needs, and excludes any prediction-market or sportsbook draft price, which is kept as a benchmark only. Slot outcomes are strongly rank-ordered at the top and diffuse in the middle, so a ranked-choice model is needed and not a per-player independent probability.
nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.measurement: Step 1: consensus score = weighted mean of z-scored ranks across at least 5 public boards and mock drafts, weight = inverse of each source's mean absolute slot error over the last 5 drafts (equal weights if history is missing), with a recency bonus for mocks published in the last 7 days. Step 2: a Plackett-Luce choice model over the remaining pool at each pick, theta_i = a * consensus_score_i + b * team_need_fit_i + c * international_or_age flag, with a, b, c fitted by maximum likelihood on the last 10 drafts (not fitted here). Step 3: simulate 20000 drafts, drawing pick order from the lottery and ownership layers, to obtain P(prospect taken at or before slot k) and P(team picks within top k). No prediction-market price, sportsbook line or Kalshi quote is an input. As-of: nightly in the final month, then hourly on draft day, with draft-night trades treated as a separate scenario.
free_sources: Tankathon (free web board and mock aggregator)
Public mock drafts and big boards (ESPN, The Ringer, others; some paywalled)

nba.single_game_margin_pmf.label: Market-free single-game margin distribution for Cup group games (ratings-implied mean, compressed tails)
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.mechanism: The Cup point-differential tiebreak needs the distribution of each remaining group game's final margin, which is a ratings-implied mean plus a spread that is compressed in blowouts when starters sit and widened by overtime-free tails.
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.rationale: The existing nba.score_resid is a residual against market lines, which is a book calibration, not an input. The tiebreak value of a margin depends on the raw margin pmf: a 20-point win counts the same in the tiebreak sum whether or not it was needed, but coaches ease off, so the margin tail is lighter than a normal distribution. The pmf is built from scores and ratings only.
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.measurement: For each remaining group game: mean margin mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (opponent-adjusted, as-of tipoff); spread = empirical distribution of final-margin residuals (final margin minus mu) from the last 5 seasons of regular-season games, giving a pmf on integer margins with sd of about 12-13 points (to be estimated, not assumed); apply the blowout compression curve from nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve to the tail. Sum margins over a team's remaining group games by convolution and rank teams with the official tiebreak order. No closing line or other price is used.

nba.deflection_rate.label: Deflections and steal-conversion rate per 36 minutes (hustle stats)
nba.deflection_rate.mechanism: A steal is a conversion of a deflection or a pass interception; deflections are a more stable measure of defensive activity than steals and predict future steals better than past steals do.
nba.deflection_rate.rationale: Steal counts are 0-3 per game with huge sampling noise; a player's deflection rate and his conversion rate (steals per deflection) separate persistent skill from luck and respond to scheme (gamble-heavy teams generate more of both).
nba.deflection_rate.measurement: Compute deflections per 36 minutes and steals per deflection from hustle-stat tracking for the last 2 seasons with 45-game half-life; shrink conversion to league mean (about 0.20 steals per deflection) with prior weight 80 deflections; expected steals per minute = deflection rate x shrunk conversion; adjust for opponent live-ball turnover propensity. As-of: games before tip.
free_sources: nba_api hustle stats (leaguehustlestatsplayer, game-level boxscorehustlev2; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for per-game availability)

nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.label: Opponent rim attempts faced while the player is the on-court rim protector, and contest/block rate
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.mechanism: Blocks equal opponent rim attempts faced times the player's contest share times block rate per contest, so block supply depends on who is the anchor and how many shots the opponent takes at the rim while he is on court.
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.rationale: Total FGA or team pace is a poor supply measure: a drop-coverage center faces 20+ rim attempts, a switching center fewer; opponent rim frequency while the player is on court, and the share of contests that are his, move block expectation more than his season blocks per minute.
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.measurement: From tracking and play-by-play compute per player: opponent rim attempts per 36 minutes on court, contest share (his contests / team contests), block rate per contest (shrunk to role prior with weight 150 contests); project tonight's rim attempts faced = opponent rim FGA per 100 possessions x possessions while on court x anchor-minutes share. Include position-pair changes when another rim protector is out. As-of: tip.
free_sources: nba_api defensive dashboard (shots defended at rim, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for per-game)

nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.label: Opponent live-ball turnover rate and primary handler carelessness
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.mechanism: Steals mostly come from live-ball turnovers (bad passes, dribbles stripped); the opponent's rate of live-ball versus dead-ball turnovers and the quality of its primary handlers set steal supply.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.rationale: Total opponent turnovers per game include offensive fouls, shot-clock and out-of-bounds events that cannot be stolen; the live-ball share and the primary handler's turnover rate are the supply for the steal contract.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.measurement: From play-by-play classify opponent turnovers as live-ball (steal-credited or bad-pass) or dead-ball; compute live-ball turnovers per 100 possessions for the opponent over last 40 games (half-life 20), shrink to league mean with prior weight 20 games; add the turnover rate of the expected primary ball handlers (from lineup) and adjust for opponent's pace. As-of: injury report.

nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.label: Dependence between steals and blocks for combined stocks, by player archetype
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.mechanism: Combined steals+blocks sums two counts whose dependence depends on defensive archetype: wings with deflection-based steals and bigs with rim blocks have small correlation, while versatile defenders have positive correlation through minutes and activity.
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.rationale: The 4+ stocks rung needs the distribution of the sum; assuming independence or perfect minutes-driven correlation misstates variance, and the covariance is archetype specific.
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.measurement: Compute the within-player correlation of steal and block counts after controlling for minutes (Pearson on Pearson residuals) over 3 seasons by archetype (guard, wing, forward, center), with Fisher-z shrinkage to archetype mean (prior weight 60 games); model sum distribution via bivariate negative-binomial or Gaussian copula with these parameters; output P(S+B >= k) for k=2..6.

nba.sl_talent_translation.label: Talent translation of rookies, two-way and G League players to a common Summer League strength scale
nba.sl_talent_translation.mechanism: Most Summer League minutes go to players without NBA data, so team strength must come from translating college, international and G League performance to an equivalent NBA-level rating.
nba.sl_talent_translation.rationale: A franchise's NBA rating says little about its Summer League roster; the strength is the minutes-weighted sum of translated player ratings, and uncertainty is large because translation factors are noisy.
nba.sl_talent_translation.measurement: For each player build a prior rating from available sources: college BPM/box-score composite (translation coefficient estimated historically by regressing NBA first-year BPM on college BPM with age and pace adjustments), G League per-minute production translated by a league-quality factor (about 0.6-0.7 estimated by backtest), international league adjustments; shrink to draft-slot prior (pick position mean) with prior weight 15 games-equivalent; team rating = minutes-weighted sum with expected minutes from announced rosters. As-of: roster announcement time.

nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.label: Probability that a drafted player or returning rotation player plays, sits or is shut down
nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.mechanism: Summer League teams manage minutes for prospects and shut down players after a few games or when they are established; the probability a top prospect plays in a given game is a decision, not an injury process.
nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.rationale: The minutes a star rookie plays varies from full to zero by team policy, game number and announcements; the market impact is large because a top pick may account for a big share of team scoring.
nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.measurement: From past Summer Leagues build a table by draft slot (1-5, 6-14, 15-30, second round), years of experience and game number of the share of games played and minutes distribution; compute shutdown hazards after game k given previous game minutes (logistic); combine with announced status via a calibrated map from announcement language (will play, game-time, shut down) to realised participation. As-of: last announcement before the order time. Two parts with different evidence: (a) the base participation and minutes table by draft slot and game number from Summer League box scores (obtainable if the box-score history is confirmed, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); (b) the map from announcement language to realised participation, which needs a live-captured timestamped archive that does not exist historically (sl-announcement-data), so part (b) cannot be fitted until captured.
free_sources: Beat-writer announcements (X/Twitter, team websites), SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for archival access

nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.label: Game importance and incentive state (tournament seeding, championship eligibility, evaluation goals)
nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.mechanism: Teams in Summer League care about evaluation and sometimes about the tournament; their minutes and effort depend on whether the game matters for seeding or the final.
nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.rationale: Win-maximizing effort is not the default: after a team is eliminated or clinched it plays deeper bench and evaluation lineups, which changes both the winner and the totals; the effect is predictable from the standings state.
nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.measurement: Compute for each team and game an indicator of seeding relevance (probability the game changes championship qualification based on standings and tiebreaks, evaluated from remaining schedule) and the team's historical bench-depth shift when eliminated; features: P(game matters), games played so far, whether prior game was a back-to-back. As-of: after the previous game's result.
free_sources: NBA.com Summer League standings and format pages

nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.label: Summer League-specific scoring, pace and margin variance baseline by format
nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.mechanism: Summer League has a different game format (quarter length, overtime rule, fouling rules) and talent level, so scoring totals, pace and margin variance differ from the regular season and must be estimated from Summer League games.
nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.rationale: Applying regular-season totals and margin sd to Summer League misstates both: games are typically higher scoring per possession with weaker defense and higher variance, so spread and total probabilities need league-specific parameters.
nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.measurement: From all Summer League games over the last 5 events compute mean total, standard deviation of total and margin, tie-at-regulation frequency, OT frequency, and pace in possessions per 40 or 48 minutes depending on format; model margin as normal with sd by league (Las Vegas, California Classic, Salt Lake City) and shrink event-level sd to the pooled value (prior weight 30 games); update with games already played in the current event. As-of: games before tip. The game length L (40 or 48 minutes) and overtime procedure are read from the event's published rules and are unconfirmed (sl-format-facts); all rates are stored per minute and scaled by L, so no format value is hard-coded.

nba.four_factors_matchup.label: Expected four factors for own offense vs opponent defense (eFG%, turnover rate, offensive rebound rate, free-throw rate)
nba.four_factors_matchup.mechanism: Team points per possession decompose into shooting efficiency, turnovers, offensive rebounds and free-throw rate; each factor responds to the specific opponent differently than the overall rating does.
nba.four_factors_matchup.rationale: Offensive rating against defensive rating is an additive approximation; a rim-heavy offense against a drop defense, or a turnover-prone offense against a pressure defense, deviates from it, and the factor-level decomposition allows shot profile, scheme and luck to enter in the right place.
nba.four_factors_matchup.measurement: For each team compute offensive and defensive four factors per 100 possessions over last 25 games (half-life 12) and season, opponent-adjusted by the standard iterative method; expected eFG = league + (own offense - league) + (opp defense allowed - league) with team-specific shrinkage weights (prior weight 20 games); combine factors into expected points per 100 using regression weights (eFG about 0.4, TOV 0.25, ORB 0.2, FT 0.15). As-of: games before tip, with lineup adjustments for absentees.

nba.joint_pace_interaction.label: Joint matchup pace from both teams' pace preferences (slower-team weight and transition vs half-court)
nba.joint_pace_interaction.mechanism: Game possessions are one shared number whose expectation is not the average of two teams' paces; a hypothesis to test is that the slower style dominates and transition-heavy teams are constrained by opponent turnovers and rebounds.
nba.joint_pace_interaction.rationale: A team's total depends on the shared possession count, so error in the pace of the matchup translates directly into points; averaging season paces misstates a matchup of a fast team vs a slow team.
nba.joint_pace_interaction.measurement: From 5 seasons of games regress game possessions on both teams' season paces (adjusted for home), their interaction and style flags (transition share, post-up share) to get weights (the weight on the slower team is a free parameter to be estimated; 0.55 is only an illustrative value, not a finding); add lineup adjustment from projected starters; residual sd by matchup type (fast-fast, fast-slow). Output expected possessions and sd. As-of: tip.

nba.team_points_variance_by_style.label: Style-dependent variance of a team's points (three-point reliance, transition share, pace)
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.mechanism: Teams that take many threes and play fast have higher game-to-game variance in points than slow half-court teams; the over/under probability at a given strike depends on the sd, not only the mean.
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.rationale: A team total strike near the mean has probability near 50% regardless of variance, but strikes at 5-10 points away depend on the sd; the sd is team- and matchup-specific and is typically 11-14 points.
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.measurement: Compute each team's residual sd of points (actual minus rating-based expectation, no market lines) over a season with regression on three-point attempt rate, pace and opponent style; shrink to league sd (about 12.5) with prior weight 25 games; combine own sd and opponent style effects; model the points distribution as skew-normal with skew from blowout probability. As-of: games before tip. Also output tail quantiles of own team points (80th, 90th, 95th and 99th percentile) and P(points >= strike) at strikes far above the mean, separately for a regulation-only and an overtime-included version, because far-away strikes (such as 135.5) are priced by the tail (three-point shooting variance, overtime) and not by the mean.

nba.team_points_margin_curve.label: Expected team points as a function of the game's expected margin (winner-loser asymmetry and garbage-time shape)
nba.team_points_margin_curve.mechanism: A team's points are not linear in the expected margin: favorites' points flatten (garbage time) and underdogs gain late points through fouling and deep-bench scoring, so the mapping from win probability to team points is a curve.
nba.team_points_margin_curve.rationale: Deriving team totals as (total ± spread)/2 assumes linearity; the empirical curve can differ by 1-2 points at large spreads, and this matters for strikes in a market keyed to the team's own points.
nba.team_points_margin_curve.measurement: From 5 seasons of games compute realised team points minus rating-based expected points as a function of pregame expected margin built from ratings (not the spread) in bins of 2 points; fit a monotone-spline of own points on expected margin with total environment as a covariate; use leave-one-season-out cross-validation; output expected team points given expected margin and total. Vintage rule: every team rating used (nba.off_rtg, nba.def_rtg, nba.lineup_adj_rating) must be the snapshot computed from games completed before that historical game's tipoff, stored daily over the 5 seasons, with the confirmed-inactive adjustment as of the pregame report; end-of-season or later-revised ratings are not allowed, as they leak the game's own result.

nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.label: Per-game tail model for a player's maximum single-game points (exceedance of 50+/54+ and overtime contribution)
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.mechanism: A highest-scoring-performance contract is the maximum over about 70 games of a heavy-tailed scoring distribution, with extreme nights requiring high minutes, hot shooting, free throws and often overtime.
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.rationale: The mean scoring rate is nearly irrelevant for 54+; the exceedance probability per game is a tail quantity that must be estimated with a peaks-over-threshold model and then compounded over remaining games (1 - (1-p)^G).
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.measurement: For each candidate fit a generalised Pareto to the exceedances of points over 35 in games with minutes >= 32 over 3 seasons, with league-wide shape shrinkage (prior weight 40 exceedances) and player-specific scale; estimate per-game P(pts >= 54) = P(game >= 35) x GPD tail beyond 54, adding an OT adjustment (OT games contribute about 6% and add about 6-8 points for stars); then P(at least one in remaining G games) = 1 - E[(1 - p)^G] with games-played uncertainty. Also track the season-to-date maximum (already achieved events resolve YES if the strike was met).

nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.label: Season-average state with rounding rule: unrounded to rounded threshold and remaining games
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.mechanism: The contract uses the rounded per-game figure from the source agencies, so the effective threshold on the unrounded average is half a rounding unit below the stated strike, and the average itself converges as games accumulate.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.rationale: A 2.6+ three-pointers per game contract resolves on the rounded value, so a true average of 2.55 counts as 2.6 (at one-decimal rounding); ignoring the rounding shifts the threshold and its uncertainty is smaller as the season progresses; zero games played counts as an average of zero.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.measurement: State = (makes to date, games played, games remaining); posterior of the player's rest-of-season average (shrunk) times remaining games plus makes to date gives the final average distribution; compute P(round(final_avg, d) >= strike) = P(final_avg >= strike - 0.5*10^-d) with d = 1 assumed from the strike precision and not confirmed by the rules (the text says only 'rounded figure as reported by the Source Agencies'; verify the decimal places and the half-up rule, sp-source-agencies), include the probability of playing zero games (settles at 0) and the denominator being games actually played. As-of: nightly after games.

nba.team_win_streak_hazard.label: Hazard of a team reaching a 20-game winning streak (run-length chain with heterogeneous game win probabilities)
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.mechanism: A 20-game win streak requires 20 consecutive wins; with game win probabilities of 75-85% for the best team, the chance depends on the full sequence of probabilities, their correlation through star health and schedule, and the number of teams that could qualify.
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.rationale: Averaging a team's win probability underestimates the chance because a streak concentrates in stretches of weak opponents and healthy rosters; the league-wide market is a union over 30 teams and 63 windows each (82 games minus 19).
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.measurement: For each team and each window of 20 consecutive scheduled games compute the product of game win probabilities from ratings and rest (with a star-health scenario mixture); P(streak >= 20 for team i) = 1 - prod over windows via a Markov chain with state = current run length; combine across teams assuming approximate independence except head-to-head links; include Cup games (they count) and exclude the Cup final and playoffs. As-of: nightly; update current runs.

nba.undefeated_start_survival.label: Survival probability of undefeated starts by calendar day (last remaining unbeaten team)
nba.undefeated_start_survival.mechanism: The last undefeated team is the one whose first loss comes latest, measured by the date of the first loss, so the market depends on survival functions of each team and ties by date.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.rationale: The product of win probabilities gives each team's survival, but the contract resolves by the day of the first loss and splits ties when several teams lose on the same day, so the probability of a team being last depends on ties and calendar clustering.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.measurement: For each team compute S_i(d) = product over games on days <= d of P(win) (from ratings, rest and home/away); P(team i is the last undefeated) = sum over days of P(i's first loss on day d and all others have lost by day d), with ties on the same day sharing 1/N; compute by simulation with dependence from shared opponents. As-of: nightly; early in the season (about 8-10 games played) the field is nearly resolved.

nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.label: Division-race state: records, remaining division games and tiebreak ledger
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.mechanism: Division winner contracts are decided by the best record in a five-team division with the league's tiebreak procedure; division head-to-head games and divisional records feed the tiebreak.
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.rationale: Division races are narrower than conference races; a tie for the best record is hypothesised to occur in roughly 10% of divisions (unverified estimate, to be computed from history) and division records are the first tiebreaker after head-to-head, so the state of divisional games matters more than overall strength.
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.measurement: For each division compute records, remaining intra-division games, head-to-head ledger and division record to date; simulate remaining season with team-strength uncertainty and apply the official tiebreak order for ties; output P(division winner) with tie contributions; update nightly. As-of: after each game.

nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.label: Probability of a specific Cup Finals pairing as the product of two conference bracket outcomes
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.mechanism: The Cup Finals pair is formed by the two semifinal winners (one from each conference bracket, if the bracket is conference-based), so the pair probability is a product of two independent single-elimination outcomes.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.rationale: The matchup contract resolves immediately upon qualification, not when the game is played; its probability depends on group results, quarterfinal and semifinal match-ups and neutral-site single-game probabilities.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.measurement: Compute P(team A reaches final) from group-stage results (qualifier probability), quarterfinal bracket draw and single-game win probabilities (neutral-site, with rest) and similarly for team B in the other bracket; P(pair) = P(A reaches final) x P(B reaches final) under independence across conference brackets (verify bracket structure from rules). As-of: nightly during the Cup. Independence across the two brackets is an approximation: if both semifinals are played at one neutral site on a shared schedule (unverified), common rest, travel and injury shocks add positive correlation, so also compute P(pair) under a copula with a correlation parameter fitted or bounded, and report the range.
